sentences.zh: 王僧達

translations.literal: Wang Sengda
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengda

sentences.zh: 王僧達，琅邪臨沂人，太保弘少子。

translations.literal: Wang Sengda was a man of Linyi in Langye, the youngest son of Grand Tutor Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengda, a native of Linyi in Langye, was the youngest son of Grand Tutor Wang Hong.

sentences.zh: 兄錫，質訥乏風采。

translations.literal: His elder brother Xi was plain and dull, lacking presence.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Wang Xi was stolid and unimpressive in bearing.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞僧達蚤慧，召見於德陽殿，問其書學及家事，應對閑敏，上甚知之，妻以臨川王義慶女。

translations.literal: The Founder Emperor heard that Sengda was precocious, summoned him to the Deyang Hall, asked about his literary studies and family affairs; his replies were easy and quick, and the emperor came to know him well and gave him the daughter of the Prince of Linchuan, Yiqing, in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder Emperor heard of Sengda's early brilliance, he summoned him to the Deyang Hall and questioned him on his studies and household affairs. Sengda answered with fluent ease, and the emperor took a strong liking to him and married him to a daughter of Prince Linchuan Liu Yiqing.

sentences.zh: 少好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved study and excelled at writing.

sentences.zh: 年未二十，以為始興王濬後軍參軍，遷太子舍人。

translations.literal: Before he was twenty he was made Rear Army Aide to the Prince of Shixing, Jun, and was promoted to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Before he turned twenty he was appointed Rear Army Aide to Prince Shixing Liu Jun, then promoted to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 坐屬疾，於楊列橋觀鬭鴨，為有司所糾，原不問。

translations.literal: Because of an illness in his household he watched duck fights at Yanglie Bridge; the authorities impeached him, but he was pardoned and not prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: While claiming illness in his household he went to Yanglie Bridge to watch duck fights; the authorities reported him, but he was forgiven and not punished.

sentences.zh: 性好鷹犬，與閭里少年相馳逐，又躬自屠牛。

translations.literal: By nature he loved hawks and dogs, raced with the young men of the neighborhood, and even slaughtered cattle himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of hawking and hunting dogs, raced with neighborhood youths, and even butchered cattle with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 義慶聞如此，令周旋沙門慧觀造而觀之。

translations.literal: When Yiqing heard of this, he sent the attendant monk Huiguan to visit and observe him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yiqing heard of this conduct, he sent the attendant monk Huiguan to call on him and see for himself.

sentences.zh: 僧達陳書滿席，與論文義，慧觀酬答不暇，深相稱美。

translations.literal: Sengda spread books across the mat and discussed literary principles with him; Huiguan could scarcely keep up in reply and praised him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Sengda had books piled across his mat and debated literary matters with him; Huiguan could barely keep pace in answering and spoke of him with high praise.

sentences.zh: 與錫不協，訴家貧，求郡，太祖欲以為秦郡，吏部郎庾炳之曰：「王弘子既不宜作秦郡，僧達亦不堪莅民。」

translations.literal: He was not on good terms with Xi, pleaded that his family was poor, and asked for a commandery; the Founder Emperor wished to appoint him to Qin Commandery, but the Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Yu Bingzhi, said: "Wang Hong's sons are already unsuited for Qin Commandery, and Sengda is also incapable of governing the people."
translations.idiomatic: At odds with his brother Xi, he pleaded poverty and asked for a prefecture. The Founder Emperor meant to give him Qin Commandery, but Yu Bingzhi, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, said, "Wang Hong's sons are already ill-suited to Qin Commandery, and Sengda is no less unfit to govern the people."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: The appointment was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太子洗馬，母憂去職。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Palace Writer for the Heir Apparent, and left office on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Palace Writer to the Heir Apparent, then left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 兄錫罷臨海郡還，送故及奉祿百萬以上，僧達一夕令奴輦取，無復所餘。

translations.literal: When his elder brother Xi returned after leaving the Linhai commandery, his parting gifts and salary amounted to more than a million cash; in one night Sengda had his slaves carry it all off, leaving nothing behind.
translations.idiomatic: When his brother Xi returned from Linhai Commandery, his farewell gifts and salary totaled more than a million cash. In a single night Sengda had his slaves haul it all away, leaving nothing.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為宣城太守。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he became Administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was appointed Administrator of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 性好游獵，而山郡無事，僧達肆意馳騁，或三五日不歸，受辭訟多在獵所，民或相逢不識，問府君所在，僧達曰：「近在後。」

translations.literal: He loved hunting by nature, and as the mountain commandery was untroubled, Sengda galloped as he pleased, sometimes not returning for three or five days; he received lawsuits mostly at his hunting grounds. When commoners met him and did not recognize him, they asked where the prefect was, and Sengda said: "He is just behind."
translations.idiomatic: Fond of hunting, and with little trouble in that mountain prefecture, Sengda rode wherever he pleased and sometimes stayed out three to five days. He heard lawsuits mostly at his hunting camps. When commoners met him and did not know him, they asked where the prefect was; Sengda replied, "Just back there."

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十八年春，索虜寇逼，都邑危懼，僧達求入衛京師，見許。

translations.literal: In spring of the twenty-eighth year of Yuanjia, the northern enemy pressed close in raid, the capital was in peril, and Sengda asked to enter and guard the capital; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Yuanjia 28 the northern foe pressed the capital, and the court was alarmed. Sengda asked to come defend the capital and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 賊退，又除宣城太守，頃之，徙任義興。

translations.literal: When the enemy withdrew he was again appointed Administrator of Xuancheng, and shortly thereafter was transferred to Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: After the enemy withdrew he was again made Administrator of Xuancheng, then soon transferred to Yixing.

sentences.zh: 三十年，元凶弒立，世祖入討，普檄諸州郡，又符郡發兵，僧達未知所從。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year the deposed heir murdered and enthroned himself; the Founder Emperor's son entered to punish him, issued a general proclamation to the commanderies and prefectures, and also ordered the prefecture to raise troops. Sengda did not know which side to follow.
translations.idiomatic: In year 30 the deposed crown prince murdered his father and seized the throne. The Founder Emperor's son Liu Jun marched to punish him, issuing a general call to the provinces and prefectures and ordering troops raised. Sengda did not know which side to take.

sentences.zh: 客說之曰：「方今釁逆滔天，古今未有，為君計，莫若承義師之檄，移告傍郡，使工言之士，明示禍福，苟在有心，誰不響應，此策上也。

translations.literal: A guest advised him, saying: "At present rebellion fills heaven, such as never was in past or present. For your plan, nothing is better than to accept the righteous army's proclamation, notify the neighboring commanderies, and send skilled speakers to make clear fortune and disaster; if any have a heart for it, who would not respond? This is the best policy.
translations.idiomatic: A visitor advised him: "Rebellion now fills the realm as never before in history. For you, the best course is to accept the loyal army's proclamation, notify neighboring prefectures, and send eloquent men to show the stakes plainly. Anyone with a conscience will answer. That is the first-best plan.

sentences.zh: 如其不能，可躬率向義之徒，詳擇水陸之便，致身南歸，亦其次也。」

translations.literal: If you cannot do that, you may personally lead those who incline to righteousness, carefully choose the convenience of water or land routes, and go south to join them yourself—that is the second best."
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot manage that, lead those loyal to the cause yourself, choose the best route by land or water, and go south in person. That is the second-best course."

sentences.zh: 僧達乃自候道南奔，逢世祖於鵲頭，即命為長史，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Sengda then went south by the post road on his own, met the Founder Emperor's son at Quetou, and was immediately appointed Chief Clerk with the additional title General Who Suppresses Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Sengda then fled south along the courier road, met Liu Jun at Quetou, and was at once made Chief Clerk with the additional rank of General Who Suppresses Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 初，世祖發尋陽，沈慶之謂人曰：「王僧達必來赴義。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Founder Emperor's son set out from Xunyang, Shen Qingzhi said to others: "Wang Sengda will surely come to join the righteous cause."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Liu Jun set out from Xunyang, Shen Qingzhi told others, "Wang Sengda will certainly come to the loyal cause."

sentences.zh: 人問其所以，慶之曰：「虜馬飲江，王出赴難，見在先帝前，議論開張，執意明決，以此言之，其至必也。」

translations.literal: When people asked his reason, Qingzhi said: "Barbarian horses drink at the river, and Wang goes out to meet the crisis. I have seen him before the late emperor: his discourse was open and bold, his purpose clear and firm. Speaking from this, he is sure to come."
translations.idiomatic: When they asked why, Qingzhi said, "With barbarian horses at the river, Wang will come to the crisis. I have seen him before the late emperor—open in debate, clear and firm in purpose. From that I say he is certain to come."

sentences.zh: 上即位，以為尚書右僕射，尋出為使持節、南蠻校尉，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, he was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and soon sent out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Colonel of Southern Man with the additional title General Who Suppresses Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Sengda was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, then soon sent out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Colonel of Southern Man with the additional rank of General Who Suppresses Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 時南郡王義宣求留江陵，南蠻不解，不成行。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Nanjun, Yixuan, asked to remain at Jiangling; the Southern Man post could not be filled, and the appointment did not take effect.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Nanjun Liu Yixuan asked to stay at Jiangling, so the Southern Man post could not be assumed and the tour never took place.

sentences.zh: 仍補護軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was then made Defender of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Defender of the Army.

sentences.zh: 僧達自負才地，謂當時莫及。

translations.literal: Sengda relied on his talent and standing and believed no one of the time could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Sengda trusted in his talent and pedigree and thought no one alive could equal him.

sentences.zh: 上初踐阼，即居端右，一二年間，便望宰相。

translations.literal: When the emperor had just ascended the throne, he already stood at the chief right hand; within a year or two he looked to become chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the emperor took the throne, Sengda stood at the chief right hand of power, and within a year or two he expected the premiership.

sentences.zh: 及為護軍，不得志，乃啟求徐州，曰：

translations.literal: When he became Defender of the Army and was discontent, he memorialized asking for Xuzhou, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Made Defender of the Army and frustrated, he petitioned for Xuzhou, writing:

sentences.zh: :臣衰索餘生，逢辰藉業，先帝追念功臣，眷及遺賤，飾短捐陋，布策稠采，從官委褐，十有一載。

translations.literal: Your subject's declining years cling to what life remains; meeting this age I rely on my inherited work. The late emperor, recalling meritorious servants, extended favor even to the lowly remnant, covering my faults and overlooking my meanness, spreading policies in thick abundance. I have followed office in plain cloth for eleven years.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject clings to what is left of a failing life and, meeting this age, rests on inherited standing. The late emperor, remembering meritorious servants, extended his regard even to the humblest remnant of our house, glossing my faults and overlooking my meanness while he showered policy upon policy. I have served in plain office for eleven years.

sentences.zh: 早憑慶泰，晚親盛明，而有志於學，無獨見之敏，有務在身，無偏鑒之識，固不足建言世治，備辨時宜。

translations.literal: Early I relied on fortunate peace; late I drew near splendid clarity. I have will to study but not the keenness of independent insight; I have duties on my person but not the discerning eye of partial judgment—thus I am truly insufficient to speak on governing the age or fully distinguish what the times require.
translations.idiomatic: Early I enjoyed fortunate peace; late I drew near your splendid reign. I wish to learn, yet lack keen insight of my own; I bear duties, yet lack the discerning eye to judge them—so I am hardly fit to counsel on governing the realm or to read the needs of the hour.

sentences.zh: 竊以天恩不可終報，尸素難可久處，故猖狂蕪謬，每陳所懷。

translations.literal: I venture to think heaven's grace cannot be repaid to the end, and holding office in idleness is hard to abide long; therefore in reckless confusion and coarse error I often state what is in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to think heaven's grace can never be fully repaid, and idleness in office cannot be borne forever; hence my reckless, clumsy words whenever I lay bare what I feel.

sentences.zh: :陛下孝誠發衷，義順動物，自龍飛以來，實應九服同歡，三光再朗，而臣假視巷里，借聽民謠，黎氓□□，未締其感，遠近風議，不獲稍進，臣所用夙宵疾首，寤寐疚心者也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's filial sincerity issues from the heart, righteousness and accord move all creatures; since the dragon's ascent it should truly be that the nine domains rejoice as one and the three luminaries shine anew. Yet your subject, by false watching in the lanes and borrowed listening to folk songs, sees the common people [text missing], their feeling not yet bound, and near and far the wind of opinion does not advance even slightly—this is what makes your subject ache morning and night and feel guilt waking and sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's filial sincerity springs from the heart, and righteous accord moves all living things; since your accession the nine domains ought to rejoice as one and the three luminaries shine anew. Yet when I watch the lanes and listen to folk songs, the common people [text missing] have not yet been won, and opinion near and far shows no improvement—this is what keeps me in anguish day and night and guilty in waking and sleep.

sentences.zh: 臣取之前載，譬之於今。

translations.literal: Your subject takes former records and compares them to today.
translations.idiomatic: I take the records of the past and set them beside the present.

sentences.zh: 當漢文之時，可謂藉已成之業，據既安之運，重以布衣菲食，憂勤治道，而賈誼披露迺誠，猶有歎哭之諫。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wen of Han, one may say he relied on an already completed enterprise and stood on a already settled fortune, and moreover wore plain cloth and ate simple food while anxiously laboring at governance—yet Jia Yi laid bare his utmost sincerity and still had his lamenting, weeping remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen of Han the throne rested on a finished enterprise and a settled age, and the emperor himself wore plain cloth and ate simple fare while laboring over government—yet Jia Yi still poured out his heart and offered the counsel that moved him to sighs and tears.

sentences.zh: 況今承顛沛，萬機惟始，恩未及普，信未遑周。

translations.literal: How much more now, inheriting turmoil, with the myriad tasks only beginning, grace not yet reaching everywhere, trust not yet able to encircle all.
translations.idiomatic: How much more now, when you inherit turmoil, when the myriad affairs have only just begun, when favor has not yet spread everywhere and trust has not yet circled the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞前達有言，天下，重器也，一安不可卒危，一危亦不可卒安，陛下神思淵通，亦當鑒之聖慮。

translations.literal: Your subject has also heard that the former worthies said: the realm is a weighty vessel; once settled it cannot suddenly be endangered, and once endangered it cannot suddenly be settled. Your Majesty's divine thought is deep and penetrating—you should also reflect on this in your sacred deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard the ancients say that the realm is a weighty vessel: once secure it must not be suddenly endangered, and once endangered it must not be suddenly secured. Your Majesty's mind is profound and penetrating—may you weigh this in your sacred deliberation.

sentences.zh: :竊謂當今之務，惟在萬有為己，家國同憂，允彼庶心，從民之欲。

translations.literal: I venture to say the task of today lies solely in making all things one's own concern, sharing worry for family and state, granting the multitude's hearts, and following the people's desires.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to say that today's task is to make all things your own concern, to share the worry of house and state, to win the people's hearts, and to follow their desires.

sentences.zh: 民有咨瘼之聲，君表納隍之志。

translations.literal: When the people have voices of bitter complaint, the ruler should show the will to take in the moat.
translations.idiomatic: When the people voice bitter complaint, the ruler should show the will to take their troubles upon himself.

sentences.zh: 下有愆弊之苦，上無侈豫之情。

translations.literal: Below there is the suffering of faults and abuses; above there is no mood of extravagant ease.
translations.idiomatic: Below lie the pains of fault and abuse; above let there be no mood of extravagant ease.

sentences.zh: 又應官酌其才，爵疇其望，與失不賞，寧失不刑。

translations.literal: Moreover offices should measure men's talents, ranks should match their expectations, and it is better to reward wrongly than to punish wrongly.
translations.idiomatic: Offices should fit men's talents, ranks should match their deserts, and it is better to reward in error than to punish in error.

sentences.zh: 至若樞任重司，藩扞要鎮，治亂攸寄，動靜所歸，百度惟新，或可因而弗革，事在適宜，無或定其出處。

translations.literal: As for pivot posts and weighty offices, frontier screens and key garrisons—on these order and disorder depend, to these movement and stillness turn. Though the hundred measures are all new, some may be left unchanged as they are; affairs lie in what is fitting, and one should not fix their coming or going in advance.
translations.idiomatic: As for pivot posts and weighty offices, frontier commands and key garrisons—on these order and disorder depend, to these action and rest turn. Though the hundred measures are all new, some may be left as they are; what matters is fitness, not fixing in advance who goes where.

sentences.zh: 天下多才，在所用之。

translations.literal: Under heaven there are many talents; it lies in employing them.
translations.idiomatic: Talent abounds under heaven; what matters is to use it.

sentences.zh: :臣非惟寄觀世路，謬識其難，即之於身，詳見其弊。

translations.literal: Your subject not only by borrowed watching of the world's path wrongly knows its difficulty; applied to my own person, I see its abuses in detail.
translations.idiomatic: I do not only, by watching the world's course from afar, misread its difficulties; applied to myself, I see its abuses in detail.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 臣雖得免牆面，書不入於學伍，行無愆戾，自無近於才能，直以廕託門世，夙列榮齒。

translations.literal: Though your subject escaped the wall-facing shame, my writings did not enter the ranks of learning, my conduct has no transgression, yet by myself I am not close to talent; I rely solely on patronage through my clan's standing and long stood among honored ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Though I escaped the shame of ignorance, my writings never entered the schools, my conduct is without offense, yet by myself I am no near match for ability; I rest only on my clan's patronage and long stood among the honored ranks.

sentences.zh: 且近雖奔迸江路，歸命南闕，竟何功効，可以書賞。

translations.literal: Moreover, though recently I rushed along the river road and submitted to the southern gate, what achievement at last can be written down for reward?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, though I lately rushed along the river road and submitted to the southern court, what achievement is there that deserves to be recorded for reward?

sentences.zh: 而頻出內寵，陛下綢繆數旬之中，累發明詔。

translations.literal: Yet favor from within the palace has issued repeatedly; within a few dozen days Your Majesty's intimate care has sent forth many bright edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet favor from within the palace has come again and again; within a few dozen days Your Majesty's intimate regard has issued many bright edicts.

sentences.zh: 自非才略有素，聲實相任，豈可聞而弗驚，履而無懼。

translations.literal: Unless talent and strategy were already formed and reputation and reality matched the charge, how could one hear this and not be startled, tread this and not fear?
translations.idiomatic: Unless talent and strategy were already formed and reputation matched the charge, how could one hear this without alarm or bear it without fear?

sentences.zh: 固宜退省身分，識恩之厚，不知報答，當在何期。

translations.literal: I should indeed withdraw and examine my station, know the thickness of grace, and not know how to repay it—when should that be?
translations.idiomatic: I ought to withdraw and examine my station, know how deep your grace runs, and wonder when I can ever repay it.

sentences.zh: 夫見危致命，死而後已，皆殷勤前誥，重其忘生。

translations.literal: To see peril and give one's life, to die and only then stop—all are earnest teachings of former ages, honoring those who forget life.
translations.idiomatic: To face peril and give one's life, to die and only then stop—these are the earnest teachings of former ages, honoring those who forget themselves.

sentences.zh: 臣感先聖格言，思在必効之地，使生獲其志，死得其所。

translations.literal: Your subject is moved by the former sages' maxims and thinks of the place where effect is certain, so that in life I may obtain my aim and in death find my due.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by the maxims of the former sages, I think of the place where I can be of certain use, so that in life I may fulfill my aim and in death find my due.

sentences.zh: 如使臣享厚祿，居重榮，衣狐坐熊，而無事於世者，固所不能安也。

translations.literal: If your subject enjoyed thick salary, dwelt in heavy honor, wore fox and sat on bear, yet had no business in the world—I truly could not be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: If I were to enjoy rich salary, dwell in high honor, wear fox fur and sit on bear skins, yet have no work in the world, I truly could not be at ease.

sentences.zh: 今四夷猶警，國未忘戰，辮髮凶詭，尤宜裁防。

translations.literal: Now the four barbarians still give warning, the state has not forgotten war, and the braided-haired foe is treacherous and cunning—especially they should be checked and guarded against.
translations.idiomatic: The four quarters still give alarm, the state has not forgotten war, and the braided-haired foe is treacherous and cunning—above all he must be checked and guarded against.

sentences.zh: 間者天兵未獲，已肆其輕漢之心，恐戎狄貪惏，猶懷匪遜。

translations.literal: Recently, though the heavenly army has not yet achieved victory, they have already let loose their heart to slight Han; I fear the Rong and Di, greedy and insatiable, still harbor unrighteous defiance.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, though our armies have not yet won, they have already shown their contempt for Han; I fear the northern peoples, greedy and insatiable, still harbor defiance.

sentences.zh: 脫以神州暫擾，中夏兵飢，容或遊魂塞內，重窺邊壘。

translations.literal: If the divine land should be briefly disturbed and the central Xia suffer hunger of troops, perhaps their roaming spirits within the passes might again peer at the frontier ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Should the sacred land be briefly disturbed and the central realm suffer hunger of troops, their roaming spirits within the passes might again peer at our frontier walls.

sentences.zh: 且高秋在節，胡馬興威，宜圖其易，蚤為之所。

translations.literal: Moreover, high autumn is at hand, barbarian horses rise in power; one should plan while it is easy and act early.
translations.idiomatic: High autumn is at hand, when barbarian horses grow bold; one should plan while matters are easy and act early.

sentences.zh: 臣每一日三省，志在報效，遠近小大，顧其所安，受效偏方，得司者則慮之所辦，情有不疑。

translations.literal: Your subject thrice each day examines himself; my will is to repay in service. Near and far, small and great, I look to what is fitting; to receive effect in one corner, to obtain an office one can manage—that is what I consider can be done, and in feeling there is no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Thrice each day I examine myself, with the will to repay your grace. Near and far, small and great, I look to what is fitting; to serve in one corner, to hold an office one can manage—that is what I believe I can do, and in that I have no doubt.

sentences.zh: 若首統軍政，董勒天兵，既才所不周，實誠亦非願。

translations.literal: If I were to head military and civil affairs and oversee the heavenly armies, it is beyond my talent and truly not my wish either.
translations.idiomatic: To head military and civil affairs and oversee the imperial armies is beyond my talent and truly not my wish.

sentences.zh: 陛下矜諒已厚，願復曲體此心。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's compassionate understanding is already thick; I beg you again to bend to this heart.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's compassionate understanding is already generous; I beg you again to bend to this wish.

sentences.zh: 護軍之任，臣不敢處，彭城軍府，即時過立。

translations.literal: The post of Defender of the Army your subject dares not hold; the Pengcheng military headquarters has just been established.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not hold the post of Defender of the Army; the Pengcheng military headquarters has just been established.

sentences.zh: 且臣本在驅馳，非希崇顯，輕智小號，足以自安。

translations.literal: Moreover your subject by origin belongs in the chase, not aspiring to lofty display; a light wit and small title are enough for self-content.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I belong by nature in the field, not aspiring to lofty display; a modest post and small title are enough for me.

sentences.zh: 願垂鑑恕，特賜申奬，則內外榮荷，存沒銘分。

translations.literal: I beg you to look down in forgiveness and specially grant my plea, then within and without will honor and bear it, living or dead engraved in duty.
translations.idiomatic: I beg your forgiveness and a special grant of my plea; then within and without all will honor your grace, and living or dead I shall be bound to you.

sentences.zh: 上不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 僧達三啟固陳，上甚不說。

translations.literal: Sengda thrice memorialized and firmly stated his case; the emperor was very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Sengda memorialized three times and held firm; the emperor was greatly displeased.

sentences.zh: 以為征虜將軍、吳郡太守。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Suppresses Barbarians and Administrator of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Suppresses Barbarians and Administrator of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 朞歲五遷，僧達彌不得意。

translations.literal: Within a year he was transferred five times; Sengda grew all the more discontent.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he was moved five times, and Sengda grew only more frustrated.

sentences.zh: 吳郭西臺寺多富沙門，僧達求須不稱意，乃遣主簿顧曠率門義劫寺內沙門竺法瑤，得數百萬。

translations.literal: At Xitai Temple outside Wu's walls there were many wealthy monks; Sengda's requests for supplies did not satisfy him, so he sent Registrar Gu Kuang leading gate guards to rob the monk Fayaou of the temple and obtained several million.
translations.idiomatic: Xitai Temple outside Wu held many wealthy monks. When Sengda's requests for funds went unsatisfied, he sent his registrar Gu Kuang with gate guards to rob the monk Fayaou of the temple and seized several million cash.

sentences.zh: 荊、江反叛，加僧達置佐領兵，臺符聽置千人，而輒立三十隊，隊八十人。

translations.literal: When Jing and Jiang rebelled, Sengda was additionally ordered to set aides and lead troops; the court document allowed a thousand men, but he promptly established thirty companies of eighty men each.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing and Jiang rebelled, Sengda was ordered to raise aides and lead troops. The court document allowed a thousand men, but he promptly formed thirty companies of eighty men each.

sentences.zh: 又立宅於吳，多役公力。

translations.literal: He also built a mansion in Wu, extensively using public labor.
translations.idiomatic: He also built a mansion in Wu, drawing heavily on public labor.

sentences.zh: 坐免官。

translations.literal: On these grounds he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 初，僧達為太子洗馬，在東宮，愛念軍人朱靈寶，及出為宣城，靈寶已長，僧達詐列死亡，寄宣城左永之籍，注以為己子，改名元序，啟太祖以為武陵國典衛令，又以補竟陵國典書令，建平國中軍將軍。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Sengda was Palace Writer for the Heir Apparent in the Eastern Palace, he was fond of the soldier Zhu Lingbao. When he went out to Xuancheng, Lingbao had already grown up; Sengda falsely listed him as dead, entered him on the register of Zuo Yongzhi of Xuancheng, noted him as his own son, renamed him Yuanxu, and memorialized the Founder Emperor to make him Commandery Guard Director of Wuling, then also supplemented him as Commandery Secretary Director of Jingling and Central Army General of Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Sengda was Palace Writer in the Eastern Palace, he favored the soldier Zhu Lingbao. When he left for Xuancheng, Lingbao had already come of age. Sengda falsely reported him dead, entered him on Zuo Yongzhi's Xuancheng register as his own son under the name Yuanxu, and petitioned the Founder Emperor to make him Commandery Guard Director of Wuling, then also secured him posts as Commandery Secretary Director of Jingling and Central Army General of Jianping.

sentences.zh: 孝建元年春，事發，又加禁錮。

translations.literal: In spring of the first year of Xiaojian the affair came to light, and he was further placed under detention.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Xiaojian 1 the affair came to light, and he was further placed under detention.

sentences.zh: 上表陳謝云：「不能因依左右，傾意權貴。」

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial of apology, saying: "I could not rely on those at the ruler's side and pour out my heart to the powerful and noble."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial of apology, writing, "I could not court those at your side and pour out my heart to the powerful."

sentences.zh: 上愈怒。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angrier still.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angrier still.

sentences.zh: 僧達族子確年少，美姿容，僧達與之私款。

translations.literal: Sengda's clansman Que was young, with beautiful looks; Sengda was on intimate terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: Sengda's clansman Que was young and handsome; Sengda was intimate with him.

sentences.zh: 確叔父休為永嘉太守，當將確之郡，僧達欲逼留之，確知其意，避不復往。

translations.literal: Que's uncle Xiu was Administrator of Yongjia and was about to take Que to the commandery; Sengda wished to force him to stay, but Que knew his intent and avoided going.
translations.idiomatic: Que's uncle Xiu was Administrator of Yongjia and was about to take Que to his post. Sengda meant to force him to stay, but Que understood and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 僧達大怒，潛於所住屋後作大坑，欲誘確來別，因殺而埋之，從弟僧虔知其謀，禁呵乃止。

translations.literal: Sengda was greatly enraged, secretly dug a large pit behind his dwelling, wished to lure Que to a farewell visit and then kill and bury him; his cousin Sengqian knew the plot, forbade and scolded him, and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Sengda flew into a rage, secretly dug a large pit behind his house, and meant to lure Que to a farewell visit, kill him, and bury him there. His cousin Sengqian learned of the plot, forbade and scolded him, and he stopped.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞劉瑀奏請收治，上不許。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Liu Yu memorialized asking that he be taken and punished; the emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Liu Yu memorialized to have him arrested and punished; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 孝建三年，除太常，意尤不悅。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaojian he was made Minister of Ceremonies, and was especially displeased in mind.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian 3 he was made Minister of Ceremonies and was especially displeased.

sentences.zh: 頃之，上表解職，曰：

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he submitted a memorial resigning office, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he submitted a memorial resigning office, writing:

sentences.zh: :臣自審庸短，少闕宦情，兼宿抱重疾，年月稍甚，生平素念，願閑衡廬。

translations.literal: Your subject examines himself as mediocre and short, with little taste for office, and moreover long harbors a heavy illness that grows worse with the years; my lifelong constant wish is to rest in seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: I find myself mediocre and brief in talent, with little taste for office, and I have long carried a grave illness that worsens with the years. All my life I have wished for quiet seclusion.

sentences.zh: 先朝追遠之恩，早見榮齒。

translations.literal: The former court's grace in recalling the distant early placed me among honored ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The former court's grace in remembering the distant early placed me among the honored ranks.

sentences.zh: 曩者以親貧須養，僶俛從祿，解褐後府，十有餘旬。

translations.literal: Formerly, because my kin were poor and needed support, I bent low to accept salary, left plain cloth for the rear office, for more than ten tens of days.
translations.idiomatic: Once, because my kin were poor and needed support, I bent low to accept salary and left plain dress for the rear office, for more than a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 俄遷舍人，殆不朝直。

translations.literal: Soon I was transferred to Attendant and scarcely attended court duty.
translations.idiomatic: Soon I was made Attendant and scarcely attended court duty.

sentences.zh: 實無緣坐閱宸寵，尸爵家庭，情計二三，屢經聞啟，終獲允亮，賜反初服。

translations.literal: Truly I had no cause to sit and watch imperial favor, holding rank idly in the family; my feelings and plans were two or three, repeatedly reported and heard, and at last I obtained approval and was granted return to my first garb.
translations.idiomatic: I truly had no cause to sit idle under imperial favor, holding rank without serving the house. Two or three times I reported my wish and at last won approval to return to private life.

sentences.zh: 還私未用，又擢為洗馬，意旨優隆，其令且拜，許有郡缺，當務處置。

translations.literal: I had not yet returned to private life when I was again promoted to Palace Writer; the intent was especially generous—ordered to accept for the time being, with promise that when a commandery vacancy arose it would be arranged.
translations.idiomatic: I had not yet returned to private life when I was again made Palace Writer. The intent was especially generous: I was ordered to accept for the time being, with promise that a prefecture would be found when a vacancy arose.

sentences.zh: 會琅邪遷改，即蒙敕往反神翰，慈誘殷勤，令裝成即自隨。

translations.literal: It happened that Langye was transferred and changed; I immediately received an edict to go there and return with the sacred brush. Kind inducement was earnest, ordering me to complete preparations and follow at once.
translations.idiomatic: When Langye was reorganized I at once received an edict to go and return with the imperial writ. Your kind inducement was earnest, ordering me to make ready and follow immediately.

sentences.zh: 靈寶往年淪覆長溪，因彼散失，仰感沉恩，俯銘浮寵。

translations.literal: Lingbao in former years was lost and overwhelmed at Changxi; through that he was scattered and lost. Looking up I felt deep grace, looking down I engraved floating favor.
translations.idiomatic: Lingbao in former years was lost at Changxi and scattered thereby. Looking up I felt your deep grace; looking down I marked your passing favor.

sentences.zh: 臣釁積禍并，仍丁艱罰，聊及視息，即蒙逮問，具啟以奉營情事，負舉猥多。

translations.literal: Your subject's offenses piled up and disasters joined; I still met with the punishment of mourning. Barely reaching the drawing of breath, I immediately received summons for questioning, fully reported to supply the facts of the case, and bore many petty charges.
translations.idiomatic: My offenses piled up and disasters joined; I still met with the punishment of mourning. Barely drawing breath, I was summoned for questioning, reported the full facts, and bore many petty charges.

sentences.zh: 賜莅宣城，極其窮躓。

translations.literal: I was granted to arrive at Xuancheng at the extreme of my stumbling.
translations.idiomatic: I was sent to Xuancheng at the lowest point of my fall.

sentences.zh: 仲春移任，方冬便值虜南侵。

translations.literal: In mid-spring I was transferred to a new post; just at winter the barbarians invaded south.
translations.idiomatic: In mid-spring I was transferred; by winter the northern foe had invaded south.

sentences.zh: 臣忝同肺腑，情為義動，苦求還都，侍衛輦轂。

translations.literal: Your subject, shamed to share the same flesh and bone, was moved by righteousness in feeling, bitterly asked to return to the capital, and guarded the imperial carriage hub.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed to share the same flesh and bone as the throne, I was moved by duty, begged bitterly to return to the capital, and guarded the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 至止之日，戎旗已搴。

translations.literal: On the day I arrived and stopped, the military banners had already been raised.
translations.idiomatic: On the day I arrived, the army banners had already been raised.

sentences.zh: 在郡雖淺，而貪得分了，方拂農衣，還事耕牧，宣城民庶，詣闕見請。

translations.literal: Though my time in the commandery was shallow, I greedily wished to divide and conclude affairs; I had just brushed off farming clothes and returned to plowing and herding when the people of Xuancheng went to the gate to petition.
translations.idiomatic: Though my time in the prefecture was brief, I wished greedily to settle affairs and had just put on farming dress to return to plowing and herding when the people of Xuancheng went to court to petition.

sentences.zh: 爾時敕亡從兄僧綽宣見留之旨。

translations.literal: At that time an edict from my deceased cousin Sengchuo announced the intent to detain me.
translations.idiomatic: At that time an edict from my late cousin Sengchuo announced the intent to keep me.

sentences.zh: 闇疾寡任，野心素積，仍附啟苦乞且旋任。

translations.literal: Dim illness and scant capacity, a wild heart long accumulated—I still appended a memorial bitterly begging to return to my post for the time being.
translations.idiomatic: Dim of illness and scant in capacity, with a wild heart long accumulated, I still appended a memorial bitterly begging to return to my post for the time being.

sentences.zh: 還務未期，亡兄臣錫奄見棄背，啟解奔赴，賜帶郡還都，曾未淹積，復除義興。

translations.literal: Before my return to duty was due, my deceased elder brother Xi suddenly was cast off and abandoned; I memorialized to be released to rush there, was granted to carry the commandery and return to the capital, and before the time had fully passed was again appointed to Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Before my return to duty was due, my late brother Xi suddenly died. I memorialized to be released to rush there, was granted to return to the capital still bearing my prefecture, and before long was again appointed to Yixing.

sentences.zh: 臣自天飛海泳，豈假鱗翼，徒思橫施，與日而深。

translations.literal: Your subject, flying in heaven and swimming in the sea by himself—how would I borrow scales or wings? I only think of what was spread across me, growing deeper day by day.
translations.idiomatic: I have flown through heaven and swum the sea by your grace—what need had I of fins or wings? I only think of what you have spread upon me, growing deeper day by day.

sentences.zh: 自處官以來，未嘗有涓豪之積，羸疾闇疚，又無人一諾。

translations.literal: Since taking office, I have never accumulated even a jot; weakened by illness and dim with affliction, I have no one to give a single promise to.
translations.idiomatic: Since I took office I have never saved even a jot. Weakened by illness and dim with grief, I have no one on whom I can rely.

sentences.zh: 而性狎林水，偏愛禽魚，議其所託，動乖治要，故收崖斂分，無忘俄頃，實由有待難供，上裝未立，東郡奉輕，西陝祿重。

translations.literal: Yet by nature I am intimate with forests and waters and especially love birds and fish; what I discuss and entrust myself to constantly misses the essentials of governance. Therefore I restrain my precipices and gather my shares and forget not for a moment—truly because what I wait upon is hard to supply: upper dress not yet established, eastern commandery salary light, western Shaanxi stipend heavy.
translations.idiomatic: By nature I am drawn to forests and streams and love birds and fish; the pursuits I choose constantly miss the essentials of governance. I must restrain myself every moment, for what I need is hard to afford—proper dress still lacking, the salary of an eastern commandery too light and that of a western post too heavy.

sentences.zh: 具陳蘄懇，備執初願，乞置江、湘遠郡，一二年中，庶反耕之日，糧藥有寄。

translations.literal: I fully stated my earnest pleas and fully held to my original wish, begging placement in distant commands of Jiang and Xiang; within one or two years, hopefully on the day I return to farming, grain and medicine will have somewhere to rely.
translations.idiomatic: I have fully stated my earnest plea and held firm to my original wish: place me in a distant Jiang or Xiang commandery so that within a year or two, when I return to the plow, I may have grain and medicine to rely upon.

sentences.zh: 即蒙亮許，當賜矜擢。

translations.literal: Having immediately received enlightened approval, You should grant compassionate approval.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I have received Your enlightened consent, grant compassionate approval of my request.

sentences.zh: :遭逢厄運，天地崩離，世蒙聖朝門情之顧，及在臣身，復荷殊識，義雖君臣，恩猶父子。

translations.literal: : Having encountered evil fortune, heaven and earth collapsed and separated; my generation received the holy dynasty's familial regard at the gate; as for my person, I again bore special recognition—though the relation was lord and minister, the grace was like father and son.
translations.idiomatic: : I met evil fortune when heaven and earth collapsed. Our house received the holy dynasty's familial regard; as for me, I again bore Your special recognition—though the relation was lord and minister, the grace was like that of father and son.

sentences.zh: 臣誠庸蔽，心過草木，奉諱之日，不覺捐身。

translations.literal: Your subject is truly dull and blocked; my heart is inferior to grass and trees. On the day I received mourning for the late emperor, I did not know I was giving up my life.
translations.idiomatic: I am truly dull and obtuse, my heart no better than grass or trees. On the day the late emperor died, I would have given my life without a thought.

sentences.zh: 單軀弱嗣，千里共氣，繼罹凶塗，動臨危盡，生微朝露，不察如絲，信順所扶，得獲全濟，再見天地，重覩三光。

translations.literal: A lone body and weak heir, a thousand li sharing breath; again suffering the cruel road, constantly facing peril to the end; life slight as morning dew, thin as silk unseen; supported by trust and obedience, I obtained complete deliverance, again saw heaven and earth, again beheld the three lights.
translations.idiomatic: Alone in body with a weak heir, a thousand li away yet sharing the same breath, I again walked the road of disaster and constantly faced death. Life was slight as morning dew, thin as unseen silk; upheld by faith and obedience I was wholly saved, and again saw heaven and earth and the sun, moon, and stars.

sentences.zh: 于時兄子僧亮等幽窘醜逆，盡室獄戶，山川嶮岨，吉凶路塞，悠遠之思，誰能勿勞。

translations.literal: At that time my nephew Sengliang and others were confined in ugly rebellion, whole households in prison doors; mountains and rivers steep, roads of fortune and disaster blocked; thoughts stretching far—who could not toil?
translations.idiomatic: At that time my nephew Sengliang and others, trapped in that foul rebellion, had their whole households shut in prison. Mountains and rivers were steep and the roads of life and death blocked—who could not labor with distant worry?

sentences.zh: 嘗膽濡足，是其分願，分心挂腹，實亦私苦。

translations.literal: Tasting gall and wetting feet was his allotted wish; dividing heart and hanging belly was also private bitterness.
translations.idiomatic: To taste gall and wet his feet was his allotted wish; to split my heart and hang my belly in worry was my private anguish.

sentences.zh: :幸屬聖武，剋復大業，宇宙廓清，四表靖晏。

translations.literal: : Fortunately the age belonged to holy martial power; the great enterprise was recovered; the cosmos was cleared; the four quarters were calm and peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: : Fortunately the age belonged to holy martial power. The great enterprise was recovered, the cosmos cleared, and the four quarters were calm and at peace.

sentences.zh: 臣父子叔姪，同獲泰辰，造情追尋，歸骨之本，欲以死明心，誤有餘辰；

translations.literal: My father, son, uncles, and nephews together obtained the grand era; tracing feelings and seeking the root of returning bones, I wished to clear my heart through death, mistakenly having remaining days;
translations.idiomatic: My father, son, uncles, and nephews together obtained this grand era. Tracing my feelings to their root, I wished to prove my heart with death and mistakenly still had days remaining;

sentences.zh: 情願已展，避逆向順，終古常節，智力無効，有何勳庸，而頻煩恩榮，動踰分次。

translations.literal: Feelings and wishes already fulfilled; avoiding the contrary and following the proper is the eternal constant—wit and strength ineffective—what achievement or merit, yet repeatedly troubled with grace and glory, constantly exceeding my rank.
translations.idiomatic: My feelings and wishes were already fulfilled. To yield the contrary and follow the proper is the eternal norm, yet wit and strength were useless—what achievement or merit had I, that grace and glory should repeatedly be heaped upon me beyond my rank?

sentences.zh: 但忽病之日，不敢固辭，故吞訴於鵲渚，飲愧於新亭。

translations.literal: But on the day sudden illness came I dared not firmly refuse; therefore I swallowed complaint at Magpie Ford and drank shame at Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: But when sudden illness came I dared not firmly refuse; therefore I swallowed my complaint at Magpie Ford and drank shame at Xinting.

sentences.zh: 及元凶既殄，人神獲乂，端右之授，即具陳請。

translations.literal: When the prime culprit was already destroyed and men and spirits obtained order, the appointment as Right-side I immediately fully petitioned against.
translations.idiomatic: When the prime culprit was destroyed and men and spirits restored to order, I immediately petitioned in full against the appointment to the Right-side.

sentences.zh: 天慈優渥，每越常倫，南蠻、護軍，旬月私授。

translations.literal: Heaven's compassion was generous, exceeding every normal rule—Southern Man and Protector General, privately appointed within ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's compassion was generous beyond every normal rule: General of the Southern Man and Protector General were privately conferred upon me within a month.

sentences.zh: 臣三省非分，必致孤負，居常輕任，尚懼網墨，況參要內職，承寵外畿，其取覆折，不假識見。

translations.literal: Your subject thrice examined my unmerited status, certain to fail in responsibility; in ordinary light duties I still feared the net and ink—how much more joining important inner office and receiving favor in the outer capital region—the taking of overturn and break needs no insight to see.
translations.idiomatic: Thrice I examined my unmerited status and knew I must fail in my charge. In ordinary light duties I still feared the law—how much more holding important inner office while favored in the outer capital? That I would be overturned and broken needed no insight to see.

sentences.zh: 故披誠啟訴，表疏相屬，或乞輕高就卑，或願以閑易要，言誓致苦，播於辭牘，誠知固陋，當觸明科。

translations.literal: Therefore I opened sincerity and began complaint, memorials succeeding one another—or begged to go from light and high to low, or wished to exchange leisure for importance—words and vows reaching bitterness spread on documents; I truly know obstinacy and rusticity will touch the enlightened statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I opened my heart and petitioned again and again—begging to descend from high to low, or to exchange an important post for a quiet one—words of bitter oath spread across my memorials. I truly know that obstinacy and rusticity must touch the enlightened statutes.

sentences.zh: 去歲往年，累犯刑禁，理無申可，罪有恒典，虛穢朝序，慚累家業，臣甘其終，物議其盡。

translations.literal: Last year and years before, repeatedly violating penal prohibitions—reason had no petition permissible, crime had its constant law; I empty and pollute the court order, shame and burden the family enterprise; your subject accepts the end, public opinion desires my exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Last year and the years before I repeatedly violated penal prohibitions. Reason allowed no petition; crime had its fixed law. I empty and pollute the court order and shame and burden my house. I accept the end; public opinion demands my exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 陛下棄其身瑕，矜其膝貴，迂略法憲，曲相全養。

translations.literal: Your Majesty abandoned my bodily flaws, pitied my knee's nobility, passed over the laws and statutes, and bent to fully preserve and nurture me.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty set aside my bodily flaws, pitied my noble lineage, passed over the laws and statutes, and bent to preserve and nurture me wholly.

sentences.zh: 臣一至之感，口此何忘。

translations.literal: Your subject's gratitude at first arrival—by this mouth how could I forget.
translations.idiomatic: Such first grace—I can never forget to declare it.

sentences.zh: 利伊恩升，加以今位，當時震驚，收足失所，本忘閑情，不敢聞命。

translations.literal: Favor of rising through grace plus the present rank—at the time I was shocked, gathered feet and lost place; original forgetting of leisure sentiment, dared not hear the command.
translations.idiomatic: Favor raised me through grace to my present rank. At the time I was shocked and lost my footing; my original wish for quiet forgotten, I dared not refuse the command.

sentences.zh: 內慮於己，外訪於親，以為天地之仁，施不期報，再造之恩，不可妄屬。

translations.literal: Inward consideration of myself, outward inquiry of relatives—we thought heaven and earth's benevolence is given not expecting repayment; grace of second creation cannot be recklessly attributed.
translations.idiomatic: Inwardly I considered myself; outwardly I asked my kin—we thought heaven and earth's benevolence is given not expecting repayment, and grace of second creation cannot be recklessly attributed.

sentences.zh: 故洗拂灰壤，登沐膏露，上處聖澤，下更生辰，合芳離蛻，遐邇改觀。

translations.literal: Therefore washed and brushed off dust, bathed in fat dew; above receiving holy grace, below again born in the era; combined fragrance leaving shell—near and far changed their view.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I washed off the dust and bathed in rich dew; above I received holy grace, below I was born again in this era. Like fragrance leaving its shell, near and far changed their view of me.

sentences.zh: 但偷榮託幸，忽移此歲，自見妨長，轉不可寧，宜其沈放，志事俱盡。

translations.literal: But stealing glory and trusting luck suddenly moved to this year; seeing myself obstruct the elder, turning unable to be at peace—I should be sunk and released, ambition and affairs altogether exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: But stealing glory and trusting luck suddenly brought me to this year. Seeing that I obstruct my elder, I can no longer be at peace. I should be cast down and released; ambition and office are altogether exhausted.

sentences.zh: :伏願陛下承太始之德，加成物之恩，及臣狂蔽未至，得於榮次自引，聖朝厚終始之惠，孤臣保不泯之澤。

translations.literal: : I prostrate wishing Your Majesty to inherit the virtue of the Grand Beginning, complete the grace of forming things; while your subject's mad block has not yet arrived, grant release from rank by my own request—holy court's thick grace from beginning to end, lone subject preserves undying favor.
translations.idiomatic: : I prostrate and wish Your Majesty to inherit the virtue of the Grand Beginning and complete the grace that forms all things. While my mad obtuseness has not yet arrived, grant me release from rank by my own request—the holy court's grace from beginning to end, and this lone subject's undying favor preserved.

sentences.zh: 夫讓功為高，臣無功而讓；

translations.literal: Yielding merit is high; your subject has no merit yet yields;
translations.idiomatic: To yield merit is noble; I have no merit yet yield;

sentences.zh: 專素為美，臣榮采已積。

translations.literal: Plain purity is beautiful; your subject's glory and color already accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: Plain purity is beautiful; my glory and honors have already accumulated.

sentences.zh: 以是求退，誠亦可愍。

translations.literal: Seeking withdrawal on these grounds is truly also pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: To seek withdrawal on these grounds is truly pitiable as well.

sentences.zh: 又妻子為居，更無餘累，婢僕十餘，粗有田入，歲時是課，足繼朝昏。

translations.literal: Also wife and children are my dwelling, no further burdens; maidservants and bondsmen a dozen or so, roughly have field income; seasonal levies enough to continue morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: My wife and children are my only dependents; I have no further burdens. A dozen or so maidservants and bondsmen bring a modest field income; seasonal levies are enough to sustain morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 兼比日眩瞀更甚，風虛漸劇，湊理合閉，榮衛惛底，心氣忡弱，神志衰散，念此根疵，不支歲月。

translations.literal: Moreover compared to other days dizziness and blindness are worse, wind vacuity gradually severe; pores should be closed, glory guardian confused at bottom, heart qi weak and feeble, spirit and mind scattered and dispersed—considering this root flaw, cannot support months and years.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover my dizziness and blindness have grown worse day by day, and wind vacuity grows severe. My pores should be closed, my vital guard is confused, heart and breath are weak, spirit and mind scattered—considering this root affliction, I cannot last months and years.

sentences.zh: 公私誠願，宜蒙諒許，乞徇餘辰，以終瑣運。

translations.literal: Public and private sincere wish should receive understanding and consent—beg to follow remaining days to end petty fortune.
translations.idiomatic: In public and private alike my sincere wish should receive understanding and consent. I beg to follow my remaining days to the end of this petty fortune.

sentences.zh: 白水皎日，不足為譬，願垂矜鑑，哀申此請。

translations.literal: White water and bright sun are insufficient as comparison—wish to bestow compassionate inspection, pity and extend this request.
translations.idiomatic: White water and bright sun are insufficient comparison—I beg You to look with compassionate inspection and pityingly grant this request.

sentences.zh: 僧達文旨抑揚，詔付門下。

translations.literal: Sengda's document's tone was elevated and lowered; edict sent to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The tone of Sengda's memorial was insubordinate; an edict sent it to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 侍中何偃以其詞不遜，啟付南臺，又坐免官。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary He Yan because his words were not deferential, memorialized to send to the Southern Administration; again stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary He Yan, finding his words insubordinate, memorialized to send the case to the Southern Administration. Sengda was again stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 頃之，除江夏王義恭太傅長史，臨淮太守，又徙太宰長史，太守如故。

translations.literal: Soon after, appointed Chief Clerk to Grand Tutor of Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, Administrator of Linhuai; again transferred Chief Clerk of Grand Preceptor, Administrator as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made Chief Clerk to Grand Tutor Prince of Jiangxia Yigong and Administrator of Linhuai, then transferred to Chief Clerk of the Grand Preceptor while retaining the same prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，遷左衛將軍，領太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Daming year 1, transferred to General of the Left Guard, concurrently Heir Apparent Vice-Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daming he was transferred to General of the Left Guard and concurrently made Heir Apparent Vice-Director.

sentences.zh: 以歸順功，封寧陵縣五等侯。

translations.literal: For meritorious return to allegiance, enfeoffed as Marquis of Ningling County, fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: For meritorious return to allegiance he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Ningling County.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷中書令。

translations.literal: Year 2, transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 先是，南彭城蕃縣民高闍、沙門釋曇標、道方等共相誑惑，自言有鬼神龍鳳之瑞，常聞簫鼓音，與秣陵民藍宏期等謀為亂。

translations.literal: Earlier, the commoner Gao Zhe of Fancheng County in Southern Pengcheng, the monk Shi Tanbiao, Daofang, and others mutually deceived one another, declaring themselves to have omens of ghosts, spirits, dragons, and phoenixes, constantly hearing flute and drum sounds; with Lan Hongqi of Moling and others they plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Gao Zhe, a commoner of Fancheng County in Southern Pengcheng, the monk Shi Tanbiao, Daofang, and others deceived one another, claiming omens of ghosts, spirits, dragons, and phoenixes and constantly hearing flute and drum music. With Lan Hongqi of Moling and others they plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 又要結殿中將軍苗允、員外散騎侍郎嚴欣之、司空參軍闞千纂、太宰府將程農、王恬等，謀剋二年八月一日夜起兵攻宮門，晨掩太宰江夏王義恭，分兵襲殺諸大臣，以闍為天子。

translations.literal: They further wanted to join Palace Guards General Miao Yun, Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant Yan Xinzhi, Staff Member of Minister of Works Kan Qianzuan, General of Grand Preceptor's Office Cheng Nong, Wang Tian, and others, plotting to attack palace gates on the night of the first day of the eighth month in year 2 at dawn, seize Grand Preceptor Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, divide troops to strike and kill various ministers, making Zhe emperor.
translations.idiomatic: They further sought to join Palace Guards General Miao Yun, Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant Yan Xinzhi, Staff Member of the Minister of Works Kan Qianzuan, General of the Grand Preceptor's Office Cheng Nong, Wang Tian, and others, planning to raise troops on the night of the first day of the eighth month in year 2, attack the palace gates at dawn, seize Grand Preceptor Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, divide forces to strike and kill the ministers, and make Zhe emperor.

sentences.zh: 事發覺，凡黨與死者數十人。

translations.literal: When the matter was discovered, altogether dozens of party members died.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was discovered, dozens of conspirators were put to death.

sentences.zh: 僧達屢經狂逆，上以其終無悛心，因高闍事陷之，下詔曰：「王僧達餘慶所鍾，早登榮觀，輕險無行，暴於世談。

translations.literal: Sengda had repeatedly been wildly rebellious; the emperor because he ultimately had no heart of reform, used the Gao Zhe affair to entrap him; issued edict saying: "Wang Sengda, favored by residual blessing, early ascended glory and view; light and dangerous without conduct, exposed in worldly talk.
translations.idiomatic: Sengda had repeatedly been wildly rebellious. The emperor, seeing he ultimately had no heart of reform, used the Gao Zhe affair to entrap him and issued an edict saying: "Wang Sengda, favored by residual blessing, early ascended to glory; light and dangerous in conduct, notorious in public talk.

sentences.zh: 值國道中艱，盡室願效，甄其薄誠，貰其鴻慝，爵遍外內，身窮榮寵。

translations.literal: Met the nation's road in hardship; whole household wished to serve; distinguished his slight sincerity, pardoned his great wickedness; ranks everywhere inside and outside, person exhausted in glory and favor.
translations.idiomatic: When the nation's road was hard, his whole household wished to serve. We distinguished his slight sincerity and pardoned his great wickedness; ranks were spread inside and outside, and he was exhausted in glory and favor.

sentences.zh: 曾無在泮，食椹懷音，乃協規西楚，志擾東區，公行剽掠，顯奪凶黨，倚結羣惡，誣亂視聽。

translations.literal: Never had the virtue of studying at the academy, eating mulberry remembering sound; yet conspired with Western Chu, ambition disturbed Eastern Region; publicly conducted plunder, visibly seized violent factions; relied on grouping with wicked, falsely confused vision and hearing.
translations.idiomatic: He never showed the virtue of the academy or gratitude for kindness received, yet conspired in the west and disturbed the eastern region; he openly plundered and visibly joined violent factions, relying on wicked groups and deceiving sight and hearing.

sentences.zh: 朕每容隱，思加蕩雪，曾無犬馬感恩之志，而炎火成燎原之勢，涓流兆江河之形，遂脣齒高闍，契規蘇寶，搜詳妖圖，覘察象緯。

translations.literal: Each time I tolerated and concealed, thinking to add cleansing—never had the gratitude of dog and horse; yet fire formed prairie blaze, trickle foretold river form; then lips and teeth with Gao Zhe, covenant with Su Bao, searched detailed sorcerous charts, spied celestial signs.
translations.idiomatic: Each time I tolerated and concealed him, thinking to cleanse him—never did he show the gratitude of dog or horse. Yet fire formed a prairie blaze and a trickle foretold a river's shape; he then joined lips and teeth with Gao Zhe, covenanted with Su Bao, searched sorcerous charts, and spied at celestial signs.

sentences.zh: 逮賊長臨梟，餘黨就鞫，咸布辭獄牒，宣言虛市，猶欲隱忍，法為情屈。

translations.literal: When the bandit chief was near execution, remaining party came to trial—all spread words in prison documents, declared empty market; still wished to tolerate and conceal, law bent for feeling.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandit chief was near execution and the remaining party came to trial, all spread words in prison documents and declared them empty market talk; still I wished to tolerate and conceal, bending law for feeling.

sentences.zh: 小醜紛紜，人扇方甚，矯構風塵，志希非覬，固已達諸公卿，彰于朝野。

translations.literal: Small villains in confusion, people fanning greatly; falsely constructing wind and dust, ambition hoping for improper desire—already reached the various ministers, clear in court and wild.
translations.idiomatic: Petty villains stirred confusion and public rumor grew fierce. Falsely raising wind and dust, he hoped for improper ambition—already known to the ministers and clear in court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 朕焉得輕宗社之重，行匹夫之仁。

translations.literal: How can I lightly treat the weight of altars and state, act the benevolence of a common man?
translations.idiomatic: How can I lightly treat the weight of altars and state and act the private benevolence of a common man?

sentences.zh: 殛山誅邪，聖典所同，戮諷翦律，漢法攸尚。

translations.literal: Execution of mountains and punishing evil—sagely canon is the same; killing slander and cutting law—Han law is honored.
translations.idiomatic: To execute evildoers on the mountain is the same in the sagely canon; to kill slanderers and cut off lawbreakers is honored in Han law.

sentences.zh: 便可收付廷尉，肅正刑書。

translations.literal: Then may he be taken and delivered to the Court of Judicial Review, solemnly corrected by written punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be taken and delivered to the Court of Judicial Review and solemnly corrected by written punishment.

sentences.zh: 故太保華容文昭公弘契闊歷朝，綢繆眷遇，豈容忘茲勳德，忽其世祀，門爵國姻，一不貶絕。」

translations.literal: Former Grand Tutor Duke Wen Zhao of Huarong Hong, covenant through dynasties, binding affection and meeting—how could we forget these achievements and virtue, suddenly cut his world sacrifice; gate rank and state marriage—not one demoted and cut off."
translations.idiomatic: Former Grand Tutor Duke Wen Zhao of Huarong, Wang Hong, bound through dynasties by covenant and tender regard—how could We forget his achievements and virtue and suddenly cut off his ancestral sacrifices? Gate rank and state marriage shall not one be demoted or cut off."

sentences.zh: 於獄賜死。

translations.literal: At prison granted death.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted death in prison.

sentences.zh: 時年三十六。

translations.literal: At the time age thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-six years old.

sentences.zh: 子道琰，徙新安郡，前廢帝即位，得還京邑。

translations.literal: Son Daoyan, relocated to Xin'an Commandery; when Former Deposed Emperor took throne, obtained return to capital.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daoyan was relocated to Xin'an Commandery. When the Former Deposed Emperor took the throne, he was allowed to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽中，為廬陵國內史，未至郡，卒。

translations.literal: In Yuanhui of Later Deposed Emperor, made Interior Administrator of Luling Principality; before reaching command, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhui era of the Later Deposed Emperor he was made Interior Administrator of Luling Principality; before reaching the commandery he died.

sentences.zh: 蘇寶者，名寶生，本寒門，有文義之美。

translations.literal: Su Bao—named Baosheng, originally of humble gate, had beauty of literary meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Su Bao, personal name Baosheng, was originally of humble birth and possessed literary talent.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中立國子學，為毛詩助教，為太祖所知，官至南臺侍御史，江寧令。

translations.literal: Yuanjia established National University, was Assistant Instructor in Mao Classic, known to the Founder Emperor, reached office as Attendant Censor of Southern Administration, Magistrate of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanjia established the National University he was Assistant Instructor in the Mao Classic, came to the Founder Emperor's notice, and reached office as Attendant Censor of the Southern Administration and Magistrate of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 坐知高闍反不即啟聞，與闍共伏誅。

translations.literal: Sit convicted of knowing Gao Zhe's rebellion but not immediately reporting—together with Zhe executed.
translations.idiomatic: He was convicted of knowing of Gao Zhe's rebellion yet failing to report it immediately, and was executed together with Zhe.

sentences.zh: 顏竣

translations.literal: Yan Jun
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun

sentences.zh: 顏竣字士遜，琅邪臨沂人，光祿大夫延之子也。

translations.literal: Yan Jun styled Shixun, native of Linyi in Langye, son of Grand Master of Splendor Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun, styled Shixun, was a native of Linyi in Langye and the son of Grand Master of Splendor Yan Yanzhi.

sentences.zh: 太祖問延之：「卿諸子誰有卿風？」

translations.literal: The Founder Emperor asked Yanzhi: "Which of your sons has your style?"
translations.idiomatic: The Founder Emperor asked Yanzhi, "Which of your sons has your style?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「竣得臣筆，測得臣文，㚟得臣義，躍得臣酒。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Jun got my brush, Ce got my writing, Yu got my righteousness, Yue got my wine."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Jun got my brush, Ce got my prose, Yu got my moral sense, and Yue got my wine."

sentences.zh: 竣初為太學博士，太子舍人，出為世祖撫軍主簿，甚被愛遇，竣亦盡心補益。

translations.literal: Jun at first was Erudite of Imperial University, Heir Apparent Attendant; went out as Chief Clerk to Heir Apparent's Pacification Army, greatly loved and favored; Jun also fully devoted mind to supplementing.
translations.idiomatic: Jun at first was Erudite of the Imperial University and Heir Apparent Attendant. He went out as Chief Clerk to the Heir Apparent's Pacification Army and was greatly favored; Jun also devoted himself wholly to assisting him.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，上不欲諸王各立朋黨，將召竣補尚書郎，吏部尚書江湛以為竣在府有稱，不宜回改，上乃止。

translations.literal: Yuanjia middle, emperor did not wish various princes each to set up faction cliques; was about to summon Jun to supplement Palace Writer—the Minister of Personnel Jiang Zhan thought Jun had reputation in the prince's office, inappropriate to return and change; emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanjia era the emperor did not wish the various princes each to form faction cliques and was about to summon Jun to fill a Palace Writer post. Minister of Personnel Jiang Zhan thought Jun had a good reputation in the prince's office and should not be transferred; the emperor then stopped.

sentences.zh: 遂隨府轉安北、鎮軍、北中郎府主簿。

translations.literal: Thereupon followed the prince's office transferred to Pacification of North, Pacification Army, Northern Center General's office Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he followed the prince's office through transfers as Chief Clerk to the Pacification of the North, Pacification Army, and Northern Center General.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，虜自彭城北歸，復求互市，竣議曰：「愚以為與虜和親無益，已然之明效。

translations.literal: Year 28, barbarians returned from north of Pengcheng, again sought mutual market; Jun opined: "In my dull view, mutual peace with barbarians has no benefit—a clear effect already established.
translations.idiomatic: In year 28 the barbarians returned north from Pengcheng and again sought mutual trade. Jun opined: "In my dull view, peace and alliance with the barbarians bring no benefit—a lesson already clearly shown.

sentences.zh: 何以言其然？

translations.literal: How do I say it is so?
translations.idiomatic: Why do I say this is so?

sentences.zh: 夷狄之欲侵暴，正苦力之不足耳。

translations.literal: Barbarian tribes' desire to invade and violently oppress is exactly because their strength is insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians' desire to invade and plunder arises precisely because their strength is not yet enough.

sentences.zh: 未嘗拘制信義，用輟其謀。

translations.literal: Never once were they restrained by binding trust and righteousness, using that to pause their plots.
translations.idiomatic: Never once were they restrained by trust and righteousness so as to pause their plots.

sentences.zh: 昔年江上之役，乃是和親之所招。

translations.literal: The river battle of former years was precisely what peace marriage invited.
translations.idiomatic: The river battle of former years was precisely what peace and alliance invited.

sentences.zh: 歷稔交聘，遂求國婚，朝廷羈縻之義，依違不絕，既積歲月，漸不可誣，獸心無厭，重以忿怒，故至於深入。

translations.literal: Years of exchanges—then sought state marriage; court's restraining righteousness hesitated without ending; already accumulated months and years, gradually cannot be deceived; beast heart without satiety, again with angry resentment—therefore reached deep penetration.
translations.idiomatic: Years of diplomatic exchange led them to seek a royal marriage. The court's policy of restraint hesitated without end; months and years accumulated until deception was no longer possible. Their beastly hearts knew no satiety; anger mounted again—and so they penetrated deep.

sentences.zh: 幸今因兵交之後，華、戎隔判，若言互市，則復開曩敝之萌。

translations.literal: Fortunately now after arms crossed, Chinese and barbarian separated by divide—if we speak of mutual market, then again opens former corruption's sprout.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately, now after arms have crossed, Chinese and barbarian are divided. If we speak of mutual trade, we again open the sprout of former corruption.

sentences.zh: 議者不過言互市之利在得馬，今棄此所重，得彼下駟，千匹以上，尚不足言，況所得之數，裁不十百邪。

translations.literal: Those debating speak only of mutual market's benefit in getting horses—now abandoning what is heavy here, getting their inferior mounts—a thousand or more still insufficient to speak of; moreover the number obtained barely not ten or hundred?
translations.idiomatic: Those who debate speak only of the benefit of getting horses from trade. Now we abandon what is weighty here to get their inferior mounts—even a thousand or more is hardly worth mention; moreover the number obtained is barely one in ten or a hundred.

sentences.zh: 一相交關，卒難閉絕。

translations.literal: Once trade relations intersect, suddenly hard to close and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Once trade relations are opened, they are suddenly hard to close and cut off.

sentences.zh: 寇負力玩勝，驕黠已甚，雖云互市，實覘國情，多贍其求，則桀慠罔已，通而為節，則必生邊虞。

translations.literal: Bandits relying on strength playing victory, arrogant crafty already extreme—though called mutual market, truly spying national sentiment; if richly granting their requests then fierce arrogance unbounded; if connecting yet setting limits then must produce border alarms.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits rely on strength and treat victory as a game; their arrogance and craft are already extreme. Though called mutual trade, it is truly spying on the state's condition. If we richly grant their requests, fierce arrogance knows no bound; if we connect yet set limits, border alarms must arise.

sentences.zh: 不如塞其端漸，杜其觖望，內修德化，外經邊事，保境以觀其釁，於事為長。」

translations.literal: Better to block the beginning gradually, stop their hope of violation; inward cultivate virtue and transformation, outward manage border affairs—preserve the borders to observe their portent—in affairs this is longer."
translations.idiomatic: Better to block the beginning and stop their hopes of encroachment; inwardly cultivate virtue and transformation, outwardly manage border affairs, and preserve the borders to watch for their provocation—in affairs this is the longer course."

sentences.zh: 初，沙門釋僧含粗有學義，謂竣曰：「貧道粗見讖記，當有真人應符，名稱次第，屬在殿下。」

translations.literal: Earlier, the monk Shi Senghan had rough learning and meaning—said to Jun: "This poor way roughly saw prophecy records—there will be a true man responding to the omen; name and rank in order belong to Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the monk Shi Senghan had some learning and said to Jun: "This humble monk has roughly seen prophecy records: a true man will respond to the omen, and name and rank in order belong to Your Highness.

sentences.zh: 竣在彭城嘗向親人敍之，言遂宣布，聞於太祖。

translations.literal: Jun at Pengcheng once narrated this to kin—the words then were proclaimed; heard by Founder Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Jun once narrated this to kin at Pengcheng; the words were spread abroad and reached the Founder Emperor.

sentences.zh: 時元凶巫蠱事已發，故上不加推治。

translations.literal: At the time the prime culprit witchcraft affair had already erupted—therefore emperor did not add investigation.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the prime culprit's witchcraft affair had already erupted, so the emperor did not pursue the matter further.

sentences.zh: 世祖鎮尋陽，遷南中郎記室參軍。

translations.literal: Heir Apparent garrisoned Xunyang; transferred Southern Center General Records Aide.
translations.idiomatic: When the Heir Apparent garrisoned Xunyang, Jun was transferred to Records Aide to the Southern Center General.

sentences.zh: 三十年春，以父延之致仕，固求解職，不許。

translations.literal: Year 30 spring—because father Yanzhi retired, firmly sought release from office—not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year 30, because his father Yanzhi had retired, he firmly sought release from office but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 賜假未發，而太祖崩問至，世祖舉兵入討。

translations.literal: Leave granted not yet departed when Founder Emperor's death news arrived—Heir Apparent raised troops to enter punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Leave had been granted but he had not yet departed when news of the Founder Emperor's death arrived. The Heir Apparent raised troops to march in punishment.

sentences.zh: 轉諮議參軍，領錄事，任總外內，并造檄書。

translations.literal: Transferred Advisory Aide, concurrently Records Officer—responsibility total inside and outside, also drafted proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Advisory Aide and concurrently Records Officer, with responsibility over all affairs inside and outside, and also drafted the proclamation.

sentences.zh: 世祖發尋陽，便有疾，領錄事自沈慶之以下，並不堪相見，唯竣出入臥內，斷決軍機。

translations.literal: Heir Apparent departed Xunyang with illness—Records Officer from Shen Qingzhi down all unable to meet face; only Jun entered and exited within the sleeping quarters, decided military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Heir Apparent set out from Xunyang he fell ill. From Records Officer Shen Qingzhi down, none could meet with him face to face; only Jun entered and exited the inner quarters and decided military affairs.

sentences.zh: 時世祖屢經危篤，不任咨禀，凡厥眾事，竣皆專斷施行。

translations.literal: At the time Heir Apparent repeatedly critically ill, unable to bear consultation on everything; all public affairs Jun exclusively decided and executed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Heir Apparent was repeatedly gravely ill and unable to consult on all matters; Jun exclusively decided and executed every public affair.

sentences.zh: 世祖踐阼，以為侍中，俄遷左衛將軍，加散騎常侍，辭常侍，見許。

translations.literal: Heir Apparent ascended throne, made Attendant-in-Ordinary; soon transferred Left Guard General, added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; declined Attendant-in-Ordinary—seen and permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Heir Apparent ascended the throne he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary; soon he was transferred to Left Guard General and given the additional rank of Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary. He declined the Attendant-in-Ordinary rank and was permitted.

sentences.zh: 封建城縣侯，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed Marquis of Fengcheng County, fief 2000 households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fengcheng County with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 孝建元年，轉吏部尚書，領驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: Xiaojian year 1, transferred Minister of Personnel, concurrently General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiaojian he was transferred to Minister of Personnel and concurrently made General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 留心選舉，自強不息，任遇既隆，奏無不可。

translations.literal: Attentive to selection and appointment, unceasing self-strengthening—trust and treatment already lofty, memorials none not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Attentive to selection and appointment, he strengthened himself without ceasing. His trust and treatment were already lofty, and none of his memorials went unapproved.

sentences.zh: 其後謝莊代竣領選，意多不行。

translations.literal: Thereafter Xie Zhuang replaced Jun in leading selection—many intents not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Xie Zhuang replaced Jun in leading selection, and many of his intended appointments were not carried out.

sentences.zh: 竣容貌嚴毅，莊風姿甚美，賓客喧訴，常歡笑答之。

translations.literal: Jun's appearance stern and severe; Zhuang's bearing very beautiful—guests clamoring with complaints, often laughed in reply to them.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's appearance was stern and severe; Zhuang's bearing was very handsome. When guests clamored with complaints, Zhuang often laughed in reply.

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「顏竣嗔而與人官，謝莊笑而不與人官。」

translations.literal: People of the time made a saying: "Yan Jun angry yet gives people office; Xie Zhuang smiling yet does not give people office."
translations.idiomatic: People of the time said: "Yan Jun scowling yet gives people office; Xie Zhuang smiling yet does not give people office."

sentences.zh: 南郡王義宣、臧質等反，以竣兼領軍。

translations.literal: Prince of Nanjun Yixuan, Zang Zhi, and others rebelled—Jun concurrently commanded the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Nanjun Yixuan, Zang Zhi, and others rebelled, Jun concurrently commanded the army.

sentences.zh: 義宣、質諸子藏匿建康、秣陵、湖熟、江寧縣界，世祖大怒，免丹陽尹褚湛之官，收四縣官長，以竣為丹陽尹，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Yixuan and Zhi's various sons hidden within boundaries of Jiankang, Moling, Hushu, Jiangning—emperor greatly angry, stripped Magistrate of Danyang Chu Zhanzhi of office, arrested four counties' chief officials—made Jun Magistrate of Danyang, added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: The sons of Yixuan and Zhi were hidden within the boundaries of Jiankang, Moling, Hushu, and Jiangning. The emperor was greatly angered, stripped Danyang Magistrate Chu Zhanzhi of office, and arrested the chief officials of the four counties. Jun was made Magistrate of Danyang with the additional rank of Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 先是，竣未有子，而大司馬江夏王義恭諸子為元凶所殺，至是並各產男，上自為制名，名義恭子為伯禽，以比魯公伯禽，周公旦之子也；

translations.literal: Earlier Jun had no sons yet; Grand Marshal Prince of Jiangxia Yigong's various sons were killed by prime culprit—to this point each produced male heirs—emperor himself made names: named Yigong's son Boqin—comparing to Duke of Lu's Boqin, son of Duke of Zhou Dan;
