translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jun had no sons yet, and Grand Marshal Prince of Jiangxia Yigong's sons had been killed by the prime culprit. At this point each produced a male heir, and the emperor himself chose names: he named Yigong's son Boqin, comparing him to Boqin, Duke of Lu, son of the Duke of Zhou;

sentences.zh: 名竣子為辟強，以比漢侍中張良之子。

translations.literal: Named Jun's son Piqiang—comparing to Han Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhang Liang's son.
translations.idiomatic: and named Jun's son Piqiang, comparing him to the son of Han Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhang Liang.

sentences.zh: 先是元嘉中，鑄四銖錢，輪郭形制，與五銖同，用費損，無利，故百姓不盜鑄。

translations.literal: Earlier Yuanjia middle, cast four zhu coins—rim and form same as five zhu—expense damaged, no profit—therefore common people did not steal and cast.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier in the Yuanjia era four-zhu coins were cast—the rim and form the same as five-zhu coins. The cost was wasteful and unprofitable, so the common people did not illicitly cast them.

sentences.zh: 及世祖即位，又鑄孝建四銖。

translations.literal: When Heir Apparent ascended throne, again cast Xiaojian four zhu.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ascended the throne, Xiaojian four-zhu coins were cast again.

sentences.zh: 三年，尚書右丞徐爰議曰：「貴貨利民，載自五政，開鑄流圜，法成九府，民富國實，教立化光。

translations.literal: Year 3, Secretariat Right Assistant Xu Ai opined: "Precious goods benefit the people—recorded from the Five Governmental Principles; opening casting flowing round—law formed in the Nine Treasuries—people rich state solid, teaching established transformation bright.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 Secretariat Right Assistant Xu Ai opined: "Precious goods benefit the people—a principle recorded since the Five Governmental Functions; opening casting and circulating round coins—law formed in the Nine Treasuries—makes the people rich, the state solid, teaching established, and transformation bright.

sentences.zh: 及時移俗易，則通變適用，是以周、漢俶遷，隨世輕重。

translations.literal: When times move customs change, then adapt flexibly to application—therefore Zhou and Han began transformation, following world light and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: When times shift and customs change, policy must adapt flexibly to fit the age. Therefore Zhou and Han each reformed their coinage, adjusting weight to the times.

sentences.zh: 降及後代，財豐用足，因循前貫，無復改創。

translations.literal: Descending to later generations, wealth abundant and use sufficient—they followed former practice, with no further reform or innovation.
translations.idiomatic: By later generations wealth was abundant and expenditures ample; they merely followed former practice, with no further reforms or innovations.

sentences.zh: 年歷既遠，喪亂屢經，堙焚剪毀，日月銷減，貨薄民貧，公私俱困，不有革造，將至大乏。

translations.literal: Years and history already distant, loss and chaos repeatedly passed through, buried burned clipped and destroyed, day by day worn away and reduced—goods thin, people poor, public and private both distressed; without reform and creation, will reach great shortage.
translations.idiomatic: As years passed and repeated wars and upheavals took their toll, coins were buried, burned, clipped, and destroyed, dwindling day by day. Goods grew scarce and the people poor; public and private coffers alike were straitened. Without reform, a grave shortage was imminent.

sentences.zh: 謂應式遵古典，收銅繕鑄，納贖刊刑，著在往策，今宜以銅贖刑，隨罰為品。」

translations.literal: He said one ought to follow the classical model, collect copper and repair casting, accept redemption and reduce punishment—as recorded in former statutes; now copper should redeem punishments, with grades set according to the penalty."
translations.idiomatic: He argued that one should follow ancient precedent, gather copper for recoining, and accept copper in lieu of corporal punishment—a practice recorded in former statutes. Copper redemption of punishments should now be adopted, with grades set according to the severity of the offense.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The imperial edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 所鑄錢形式薄小，輪郭不成就。

translations.literal: The coins cast were thin and small in form, their rims poorly formed.
translations.idiomatic: The coins cast were thin and small, with rims poorly formed.

sentences.zh: 於是民間盜鑄者雲起，雜以鉛錫，並不牢固。

translations.literal: Thereupon illicit casters among the people rose like clouds, mixing in lead and tin—all not solid.
translations.idiomatic: Illicit casters sprang up everywhere among the people, mixing in lead and tin so that the coins were not sound.

sentences.zh: 又剪鑿古錢，以取其銅，錢轉薄小，稍違官式。

translations.literal: Again they clipped and chiseled old coins to take their copper—coins turned thin and small, slightly departing from the official standard.
translations.idiomatic: People also clipped and filed old coins to extract their copper, so that coins grew ever thinner and smaller, gradually deviating from the official standard.

sentences.zh: 雖重制嚴刑，民吏官長坐死免者相係，而盜鑄彌甚，百物踊貴，民人患苦之。

translations.literal: Although heavy laws and severe punishments were imposed—commoners, clerks, and magistrates punished with death or dismissal linked in succession—yet illicit casting grew ever worse; all goods leaped in price, and the people groaned in suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Though heavy laws and severe punishments were imposed—commoners, clerks, and magistrates executed or dismissed in unbroken succession—illicit casting grew ever worse. The price of all goods soared, and the people suffered bitterly.

sentences.zh: 乃立品格，薄小無輪郭者，悉加禁斷。

translations.literal: Thereupon grades and standards were established—thin and small coins without rims were all strictly forbidden and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Grades and standards were established, and thin coins without rims were entirely banned.

sentences.zh: 始興郡公沈慶之立議曰：「昔秦幣過重，高祖是患，普令民鑄，改造榆莢，而貨輕物重，又復乖時。

translations.literal: Duke of Shixing Shen Qingzhi submitted a proposal, saying: "Formerly Qin currency was too heavy—a plague on Gaozu of Han, who ordered universal private casting and reformed the currency into elm-seed coins; yet money grew too light and goods too dear, again out of step with the times.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Shixing Shen Qingzhi submitted a proposal: "In antiquity Qin coins were too heavy—a plague on Gaozu of Han, who ordered universal private casting and reformed the currency into elm-seed coins; yet money grew too light and goods too dear, again out of step with the age.

sentences.zh: 太宗放鑄，賈誼致譏，誠以采山術存，銅多利重，耕戰之器，曩時所用，四民競造，為害或多。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen opened casting to private hands, drawing Jia Yi's censure—for mining still flourished, copper was plentiful and profits large, and the implements of farming and warfare that times past had used were now hoarded by all four classes of society competing to cast coins, to great harm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen opened casting to private hands, drawing Jia Yi's censure—for mining still flourished, copper was plentiful and profits large, and the implements of farming and warfare that had once been essential were now hoarded by all four classes of society competing to cast coins, to great harm.

sentences.zh: 而孝文弗納，民鑄遂行，故能朽貫盈府，天下殷富。

translations.literal: Yet Emperor Wen did not adopt it—people's casting then proceeded, therefore able to rot strings filling treasuries; all under heaven grew abundant and rich.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Emperor Wen did not heed such objections; private casting went ahead, and strings of coins rotted in overflowing treasuries—the realm grew wealthy.

sentences.zh: 況今耕戰不用，采鑄廢久，鎔冶所資，多因成器，功艱利薄，絕吳、鄧之資，農民不習，無釋耒之患。

translations.literal: Moreover today farming and warfare are not used; mining and casting have long been abandoned. What smelting and refining rely on is mostly already finished vessels—the labor is hard and the profit slim. This would cut off the resources of Wu and Deng; farmers are unskilled at casting, and there is no danger of their abandoning the plow.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover farming and warfare no longer depend on copper; mining and minting have long been abandoned. What smelters draw on is mostly already-wrought vessels—the labor is hard and the profit slim. This would cut off the resources of places like Wu and Deng. Farmers are unskilled at casting, and there is no danger of their abandoning the plow.

sentences.zh: 方今中興開運，聖化惟新，雖復偃甲銷戈，而倉庫未實，公私所乏，唯錢而已。

translations.literal: Just now the dynasty has been restored and a new reign begun; though arms are sheathed and spears melted down, granaries remain unfilled, and what public and private coffers lack is coin alone.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty has been restored and a new reign begun; though arms are sheathed and spears melted down, granaries remain unfilled and what both public and private coffers lack is coin alone.

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜聽民鑄錢，郡縣開置錢署，樂鑄之家，皆居署內，平其准式，去其雜偽，官斂輪郭，藏之以為永寶。

translations.literal: I humbly think one ought to permit people to cast coins—commanderies and counties should open and establish coin offices; households pleased to cast should all reside within those offices, standards equalized and counterfeits eliminated; the government should collect the rims and store them as everlasting treasure.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly propose permitting private coinage: commanderies and counties should open mint offices; households willing to cast should all reside within those offices. Standards should be equalized and counterfeits eliminated; the government should collect the rims and store them as permanent reserves.

sentences.zh: 去春所禁新品，一時施用，今鑄悉依此格。

translations.literal: The new coins forbidden last spring should be put back into circulation for a time; all casting should now follow that standard.
translations.idiomatic: The new coins banned last spring should be put back into circulation for a time; all casting should now follow that standard.

sentences.zh: 萬稅三千，嚴檢盜鑄，并禁剪鑿。

translations.literal: Of every ten thousand coins cast, three thousand should be taxed; illicit casting should be strictly inspected, and clipping and chiseling forbidden as well.
translations.idiomatic: Of every ten thousand coins cast, three thousand should be taxed; illicit casting should be strictly inspected, and clipping and filing forbidden as well.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，公私豐贍，銅盡事息，姦偽自止。

translations.literal: Within several years public and private coffers would be abundant and sufficient; when copper was exhausted the affair would cease, and deceit and counterfeiting would naturally stop.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years public and private coffers would be ample; when copper was exhausted the matter would end, and fraud would cease of its own accord.

sentences.zh: 且禁鑄則銅轉成器，開鑄則器化為財，翦華利用，於事為益。」

translations.literal: Moreover, when casting is forbidden copper turns into vessels; when casting is opened vessels change into wealth—trimming ornament and putting resources to use would benefit the affair."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when casting is forbidden copper becomes vessels; when casting is opened vessels become wealth. Trimming excess and putting resources to use would benefit the state."

sentences.zh: 上下其事公卿，太宰江夏王義恭議曰：「伏見沈慶之議，『聽民私鑄，樂鑄之室，皆入署居。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the public ministers. Grand Tutor Prince of Jiangxia Yigong opined: "I humbly see Shen Qingzhi's proposal: 'Permit people's private casting; households pleased to cast should all enter offices to reside.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the ministers. Grand Tutor Prince of Jiangxia Yigong opined: "I have read Shen Qingzhi's proposal: 'Permit private casting; households willing to cast should all enter the mint offices to reside.

sentences.zh: 平其準式，去其雜偽』。

translations.literal: Equalize their standards and forms, remove their mixed counterfeit.'"
translations.idiomatic: Equalize standards and eliminate counterfeits.'"

sentences.zh: 愚謂百姓不樂與官相關，由來甚久，又多是人士，蓋不願入署。

translations.literal: I foolishly think common people do not delight in dealing with the government—since antiquity this has been so for a very long time; moreover many are gentry and scholars, and probably would be unwilling to enter the offices.
translations.idiomatic: I consider that the common people have long been unwilling to deal with the government—and most illicit casters are gentry who would scarcely wish to enter a mint office.

sentences.zh: 凡盜鑄為利，利在偽雜，偽雜既禁，樂入必寡。

translations.literal: Generally illicit casting is for profit—the profit lies in mixed counterfeit; once mixed counterfeit is forbidden, those pleased to enter will necessarily be few.
translations.idiomatic: The profit in illicit casting lies in adulteration; once adulteration is forbidden, few will willingly enter the offices.

sentences.zh: 云『斂取輪郭，藏為永寶』。

translations.literal: It says 'Collect and take the rims, store them as everlasting treasure.'
translations.idiomatic: As for the proposal to 'collect the rims and store them as permanent reserves'—

sentences.zh: 愚謂上之所貴，下必從之，百姓聞官斂輪郭，輪郭之價百倍，大小對易，誰肯為之。

translations.literal: I foolishly think what above values, below necessarily follows—if common people hear the government collects rims, rim prices will rise a hundredfold; with large and small coins exchanged at such rates, who would be willing to do it?
translations.idiomatic: what the court favors the people will surely pursue. If the people hear that the government collects rims, rim prices will rise a hundredfold; with large and small coins exchanged at such rates, who would comply?

sentences.zh: 強制使換，則狀似逼奪。

translations.literal: Forcing them to exchange would then resemble coercion and seizure.
translations.idiomatic: Compelling exchange would look like outright confiscation.

sentences.zh: 又『去春所禁新品，一時施用』。

translations.literal: Again, 'Last spring's forbidden new products—for a time put to use.'
translations.idiomatic: As for 'putting last spring's banned new coins back into circulation for a time'—

sentences.zh: 愚謂此條在可開許。

translations.literal: I foolishly think this item can be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: I consider this point acceptable.

sentences.zh: 又云『今鑄宜依此格，萬稅三千』。

translations.literal: Again it says 'Now casting ought follow this standard, of ten thousand tax three thousand.'
translations.idiomatic: As for 'all casting should follow this standard with a tax of three thousand per ten thousand'—

sentences.zh: 又云『嚴檢盜鑄，不得更造』。

translations.literal: Again it says 'Strictly inspect illicit casting, must not again make.'
translations.idiomatic: and 'strict inspection to forbid illicit casting'—

sentences.zh: 愚謂禁制之設，非惟一旦，昧利犯憲，羣庶常情，不患制輕，患在冒犯。

translations.literal: I foolishly think prohibitions are established—not only in a single morning; coveting profit and violating law is the multitude's common sentiment—the worry is not that regulations are too light, but that violations persist.
translations.idiomatic: prohibitions are not established overnight. The multitude's common habit is to chase profit in defiance of law—the worry is not that penalties are too light but that violations persist.

sentences.zh: 今入署必萬輸三千，私鑄無十三之稅，逐利犯禁，居然不斷。

translations.literal: Now entering the offices necessarily means of ten thousand submitting three thousand—private casting pays no such thirty-percent tax; pursuing profit and violating prohibition plainly will not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the offices means paying three thousand per ten thousand, while private casting pays no such thirty-percent tax—profit-seeking violations will plainly continue unabated.

sentences.zh: 又云『銅盡事息，姦偽自禁』。

translations.literal: Again it says 'When copper is exhausted the affair ceases, deceit and counterfeit naturally forbidden.'
translations.idiomatic: As for 'when copper is exhausted the matter ends and fraud ceases of its own accord'—

sentences.zh: 愚謂赤縣內銅，非可卒盡，比及銅盡，姦偽已積。

translations.literal: I foolishly think copper within the Red Territories cannot be suddenly exhausted; by the time copper is exhausted, deceit and counterfeit will already have accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: copper within the empire cannot be suddenly exhausted; long before it runs out, fraud will have piled up.

sentences.zh: 又云『禁鑄則銅轉成器，開鑄則器化為財』。

translations.literal: Again it says 'Forbid casting then copper turns into vessels; open casting then vessels change into wealth.'
translations.idiomatic: As for 'forbidding casting turns copper into vessels, opening casting turns vessels into wealth'—

sentences.zh: 然頃所患，患於形式不均，加以剪鑿，又鉛錫眾雜止於盜鑄銅者，亦無須苦禁。」

translations.literal: Yet recently what was afflicted was unequal form and standard, adding clipping and chiseling; again lead and tin variously mixed is limited to illicit copper casters—there is also no need for bitter prohibition."
translations.idiomatic: our recent troubles lie in unequal coin standards and clipping and filing, while adulteration with lead and tin is limited to illicit casters—there is no need for harsh prohibitions on that score either."

sentences.zh: 竣議曰：「泉貨利用，近古所同，輕重之議，定於漢世，魏、晉以降，未之能改。

translations.literal: Jun opined: "Spring goods and currency's use and benefit—near antiquity shared alike; debate over light and heavy was fixed in the Han era—from Wei and Jin descending, none could change it.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun opined: "The utility of currency has been a shared concern since antiquity. Debates over weight and denomination were settled in Han times, and from Wei and Jin onward none could alter that settlement.

sentences.zh: 誠以物貨既均，改之偽生故也。

translations.literal: Truly because goods and currency are already equal, changing them makes counterfeiting arise—therefore.
translations.idiomatic: Truly, once goods and currency are in balance, any change breeds counterfeiting.

sentences.zh: 世代漸久，弊運頓至，因革之道，宜有其術。

translations.literal: Generations and eras gradually lengthen, corrupt fortune suddenly arrives—the path of innovation and reform ought to have its methods.
translations.idiomatic: As generations pass, decay arrives suddenly, and the path of reform ought to have its methods.

sentences.zh: 今云開署放鑄，誠所欣同。

translations.literal: Now saying open offices and release casting—truly what I delight to agree with.
translations.idiomatic: Opening mint offices to private casting is something I would gladly support.

sentences.zh: 但慮採山事絕，器用日耗，銅既轉少，器亦彌貴。

translations.literal: Only I worry that mining mountains has ended, vessels and implements are daily depleted—copper already turning fewer, vessels also ever costlier.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I worry that with mining ceased and daily depletion of vessels and implements, copper grows scarce and vessels ever costlier.

sentences.zh: 設器直一千，則鑄之減半，為之無利，雖令不行。

translations.literal: Suppose a vessel worth one thousand—then casting it is halved, doing this without profit; though ordered, it will not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: If a vessel worth a thousand cash were melted down for coin, only half its value could be recouped—there is no profit, and the order would not be obeyed.

sentences.zh: 又云『去春所禁，一時施用』。

translations.literal: Again it says 'Last spring forbidden—for a time put to use.'
translations.idiomatic: As for 'putting last spring's banned coins back into circulation for a time'—

sentences.zh: 是欲使天下豐財。

translations.literal: This is wishing to make all under heaven abundant in wealth.
translations.idiomatic: that is meant to enrich the realm.

sentences.zh: 若細物必行，而不從公鑄，利已既深，情偽無極，私鑄剪鑿，盡不可禁，五銖半兩之屬，不盈一年，必至於盡。

translations.literal: Yet if small products must proceed and one does not follow public casting—profit already deep, sentiment and counterfeit without limit, private casting clipping and chiseling all cannot be forbidden; five-zhu and half-liang types, within not a full year, will necessarily reach exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if light coins must circulate while casting is left to private hands, profits will run deep and fraud without limit—private casting, clipping, and filing will be wholly unstoppable, and five-zhu and half-liang coins will within a year be utterly exhausted.

sentences.zh: 財貨未贍，大錢已竭，數歲之間，悉為塵土，豈可令取弊之道，基於皇代。

translations.literal: Wealth and goods not yet sufficient, large coins already exhausted—within several years all become dust and soil; how can one let adopting corrupt ways be founded upon the imperial era?
translations.idiomatic: Before new wealth is amassed the large coins will be spent—within a few years all will be dust. How can a policy of ruin become the foundation of our dynasty?

sentences.zh: 今百姓之貨，雖為轉少，而市井之民，未有嗟怨，此新禁初行，品式未一，須臾自止，不足以垂聖慮。

translations.literal: Now common people's goods, though turning somewhat fewer, yet market-town people have not yet sighed in complaint; this new prohibition has just begun, grades and standards not uniform—momentarily it will naturally cease, not sufficient to reach sagely concern.
translations.idiomatic: Though the people's coin has grown somewhat scarcer, market folk have not yet complained. The new ban has only just begun and standards are not yet uniform—the disorder will soon cease on its own and does not warrant the sage ruler's concern.

sentences.zh: 唯府藏空匱，實為重憂。

translations.literal: Only government treasuries empty and exhausted—truly is heavy worry.
translations.idiomatic: Only the emptiness of the government coffers is a grave worry.

sentences.zh: 今縱行細錢，官無益賦之理，百姓雖贍，無解官乏。

translations.literal: Now even if small coins proceed, the government has no principle of increased revenue—though common people are sufficient, it will not resolve the government's shortage.
translations.idiomatic: Even if light coins were circulated, there is no principle by which the government would gain revenue; though the people might be supplied, it would not relieve the government's shortage.

sentences.zh: 唯簡費去華，設在節儉，求贍之道，莫此為貴。

translations.literal: Only simplify expense, remove ornament, establish frugality—in seeking sufficiency's way, none is more honored than this.
translations.idiomatic: Only to cut expenditure, remove extravagance, and establish frugality—is there any nobler path to sufficiency.

sentences.zh: 然錢有定限，而消失無方，剪鑄雖息，終致窮盡者，亡應官開取銅之署，絕器用之塗，定其品式，日月漸鑄，歲久之後，不為世益耳。」

translations.literal: Yet coins have fixed limits, yet vanishing without method—clipping and casting though ceases, ultimately reaching exhaustion; there is no use in government opening copper-gathering offices, cutting off vessels and implements' path, fixing grades and standards, day by month gradually casting—years later, not for the world's benefit only."
translations.idiomatic: Yet coin has fixed limits while its disappearance has no bound; though clipping and illicit casting may cease, it will ultimately be exhausted. The answer is not to open government copper offices, block the supply of vessels and implements, fix standards, and cast gradually month by month—in a few years that would benefit the world not at all."

sentences.zh: 時議者又以銅轉難得，欲鑄二銖錢。

translations.literal: At the time debaters again, finding copper increasingly hard to obtain, wished to cast two-zhu coins.
translations.idiomatic: At the time some debaters, finding copper increasingly hard to obtain, proposed casting two-zhu coins.

sentences.zh: 竣又議曰：「議者將為官藏空虛，宜更改鑄，天下銅少，宜減錢式，以救交弊，賑國紓民。

translations.literal: Jun again opined: "Debaters will say government storehouses are empty and hollow—ought to change and recast; all under heaven copper is few—ought to reduce coin standard, to save intersecting corruption, relieve the state and soothe the people.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun again opined: "The debaters hold that the treasury is empty and coin should be recast; copper is scarce empire-wide and the coin standard should be reduced to rescue monetary disorder and relieve the state and people.

sentences.zh: 愚以為不然。

translations.literal: I foolishly think this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: I consider this wrong.

sentences.zh: 今鑄二銖，恣行新細，於官無解於乏，而民姦巧大興，天下之貨，將靡碎至盡。

translations.literal: Now casting two zhu, letting new thin coins proceed freely— for the government no resolving the shortage, yet among the people deceit and craft greatly rising; all under heaven's goods will be ground to fragments until exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Casting two-zhu coins now and letting new thin coins circulate freely would not relieve the government's shortage, while popular fraud would flourish and the realm's currency would be ground to fragments until nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 空立嚴禁，而利深難絕，不過一二年間，其弊不可復救。

translations.literal: Empty erecting strict prohibitions, yet profit deep and hard to cut off—not beyond one or two years, its corruption cannot again be saved.
translations.idiomatic: Empty prohibitions would be erected while deep profits made them impossible to stop; within a year or two the damage would be beyond repair.

sentences.zh: 其甚不可一也。

translations.literal: This is the first great impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first great objection.

sentences.zh: 今鎔鑄獲利，不見有頓得一二億之理，縱復得此，必待彌年。

translations.literal: Now smelting and casting profit—one does not see principle of suddenly gaining one or two hundred million; even if one obtained this, it must wait full years.
translations.idiomatic: Profit from smelting and casting offers no prospect of suddenly gaining one or two hundred million; even if obtained, it would take years.

sentences.zh: 歲暮稅登，財幣暫革，日用之費，不贍數月，雖權徵助，何解乏邪，徒使姦民意騁，而貽厥愆謀。

translations.literal: Year-end taxes collected, wealth and currency briefly changed—daily use's expenses, not sufficient for several months; though temporary levies assist, what shortage do they resolve? Only making deceitful people's intent run free, and bequeathing blameworthy policies.
translations.idiomatic: Year-end taxes are collected and revenue briefly changes, but daily expenses cannot be covered for even a few months. What shortage would temporary levies relieve? They would only unleash fraudsters' schemes and bequeath blameworthy policies.

sentences.zh: 此又甚不可二也。

translations.literal: This again is the second great impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second great objection.

sentences.zh: 民懲大錢之改，兼畏近日新禁，市井之間，必生喧擾，遠利未聞，切患猥及，富商得志，貧民困窘。

translations.literal: People chastened by large coins' change, also fearing recent new prohibitions—among market towns clamor and disturbance will necessarily arise; distant profit not yet heard, immediate affliction abundantly reaching; rich merchants get their wish, poor people distressed and trapped.
translations.idiomatic: The people, chastened by past changes to large coins and fearful of recent new prohibitions, would stir up clamor in the markets. Distant benefits are unheard of while immediate troubles abound—the rich would prevail and the poor be crushed.

sentences.zh: 此又甚不可三也。

translations.literal: This again is the third great impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third great objection.

sentences.zh: 若使交益深重，尚不可行，況又未見其利，而眾弊如此，失算當時，取誚百代乎。」

translations.literal: If even making exchange increasingly deep and heavy still cannot proceed, how much less when one has not yet seen its profit, yet many corruptions are such—miscalculation for the age, drawing ridicule for a hundred generations?"
translations.idiomatic: If even a deeply beneficial exchange were still unworkable, how much less this, whose benefits are unseen and whose evils are so many—a miscalculation for the age and a laughingstock for a hundred generations."

sentences.zh: 前廢帝即位，鑄二銖錢，形式轉細。

translations.literal: When the Former Deposed Emperor ascended the throne, two-zhu coins were cast, form turning ever thinner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Former Deposed Emperor ascended the throne, two-zhu coins were cast, ever thinner in form.

sentences.zh: 官錢每出，民間即模効之，而大小厚薄，皆不及也。

translations.literal: Whenever official coins issued, among the people they immediately copied them—yet in size, thickness, and weight all fell short.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever official coins were issued, the people immediately copied them, but in size, thickness, and weight they fell short.

sentences.zh: 無輪郭，不磨鑢，如今之剪鑿者，謂之耒子。

translations.literal: Without rims, unpolished and unfiled—like today's clipped and chiseled coins—they were called leizi.
translations.idiomatic: Without rims, unpolished and unfiled—like today's clipped coins—they were called leizi.

sentences.zh: 景和元年，沈慶之啟通私鑄，由是錢貨亂敗，一千錢長不盈三寸，大小稱此，謂之鵝眼錢。

translations.literal: First year of Jinghe, Shen Qingzhi memorialized to open private casting—thereby currency and goods chaotic and ruined; one thousand coins strung together not full three inches, large and small according to this, called goose-eye coins.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jinghe, Shen Qingzhi memorialized to permit private casting, and currency fell into chaos. A thousand coins strung together measured less than three inches; coins of this size were called "goose-eye" coins.

sentences.zh: 劣於此者，謂之綖環錢。

translations.literal: Inferior to these were called thread-ring coins.
translations.idiomatic: Those inferior to these were called "thread-ring" coins.

sentences.zh: 入水不沉，隨手破碎，市井不復料數，十萬錢不盈一掬，斗米一萬，商貨不行。

translations.literal: Put in water they did not sink; at a touch of the hand they shattered—market towns no longer measured by count; one hundred thousand coins not full one handful; one peck of rice ten thousand, commerce and goods did not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: They would not sink in water and crumbled at a touch. Markets no longer counted by measure—a hundred thousand coins did not fill a handful; a peck of rice cost ten thousand, and commerce ceased.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，唯禁鵝眼、綖環，其餘皆通用。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Xiaowu, only goose-eye and thread-ring were forbidden; the rest all generally circulated.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's reign, only goose-eye and thread-ring coins were banned; the rest remained in circulation.

sentences.zh: 復禁民鑄，官署亦廢工，尋復並斷，唯用古錢。

translations.literal: Again forbade people's casting; government offices also abandoned work—soon again all cut off, only using old coins.
translations.idiomatic: Private casting was again forbidden, the government mints also shut down, and soon all new coinage was halted—only old coins were used.

sentences.zh: 竣自散騎常侍、丹陽尹，加中書令，丹陽尹如故。

translations.literal: Jun, from Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Magistrate of Danyang, was additionally made Director of the Secretariat; Magistrate of Danyang as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun, who had been Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Magistrate of Danyang, was additionally appointed Director of the Secretariat while retaining the magistracy.

sentences.zh: 表讓中書令曰：「虛竊國靈，坐玷禁要，聞命慚惶，形魂震越。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial declining the Directorate of the Secretariat, saying: "I have undeservedly stolen the state's grace and undeservedly occupy a forbidden key post; hearing the order I am ashamed and alarmed, body and soul trembling.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial declining the Directorate: "I have undeservedly stolen the state's grace and undeservedly occupy a forbidden key post. Hearing the order I am ashamed and alarmed, my body and soul trembling.

sentences.zh: 臣東州凡鄙，生於微族，長自閭閻，不窺官轍，門無富貴，志絕華伍。

translations.literal: Your servant is a crude man of the eastern provinces, born of a humble clan, raised in the lanes, never glimpsing the ways of office; my gate knows no wealth or eminence, my ambition shuns gilded ranks.
translations.idiomatic: I am a crude man of the eastern provinces, born of a humble clan, raised in the lanes, never glimpsing the ways of office. My house knows no wealth or eminence; my ambition shuns gilded ranks.

sentences.zh: 直以委身壟畝，飢寒交切，先朝陶均庶品，不遺愚賤，得免耕稅之勤，厠仕進之末。

translations.literal: Only because I devoted myself to the fields, hunger and cold pressing upon me—the former court harmonized all classes and did not overlook the foolish and lowly, sparing me the toil of farming and taxes and allowing me a foot on the ladder of office.
translations.idiomatic: Having devoted myself to the fields, hunger and cold pressing upon me, the former court harmonized all classes and did not overlook the foolish and lowly, sparing me the toil of farming and taxes and allowing me a foot on the ladder of office.

sentences.zh: 陛下盛德居蕃，總攬英異，越以不才，超塵清軌，奉躬歷稔，勞效莫書，仰恃曲成之仁，畢願守宰之秩。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty's splendid virtue held the frontier fief and gathered the outstanding, you raised my unworthy self above the dust into the clear path of service; these many years I have served, my labors cannot be recorded—I relied on your gracious cultivation and wished only to complete my term as a local magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty's splendid virtue held the frontier fief and gathered the outstanding, you raised my unworthy self above the dust into the clear path of service. These many years I have served; my labors cannot be recorded. I relied on your gracious cultivation and wished only to complete my term as a local magistrate.

sentences.zh: 豈期天地中闋，殷憂啟聖，倚附興運，擢景神塗，雲飛海泳，冠絕倫等，曾未三朞，殊命八萃。

translations.literal: Who could expect heaven and earth to falter, deep grief to summon a sage, and by clinging to the rising fortune to be lifted to a divine height—soaring like clouds, swimming like fish, surpassing all peers? In less than three years, eight extraordinary appointments have been heaped upon me.
translations.idiomatic: Who could expect heaven and earth to falter, deep grief to summon a sage, and by clinging to the rising fortune to be lifted to a divine height—soaring like clouds, swimming like fish, surpassing all peers? In less than three years, eight extraordinary appointments have been heaped upon me.

sentences.zh: 詳料賞典，則臣不應科；

translations.literal: Weighing the standards of reward, your servant does not qualify;
translations.idiomatic: Weighing the standards of reward, I do not qualify;

sentences.zh: 瞻言勤良，則臣與侔貴。

translations.literal: considering the diligent and worthy, your servant stands among the noble.
translations.idiomatic: considering the diligent and worthy, I stand among the noble.

sentences.zh: 方欲訴款皇朝，降階盛序，微已國言，少徹身謗，而制書猥下，爵樹彌隆。

translations.literal: I had meant to plead my sincerity before the court, step down from lofty rank, diminish the state's words about me, and slightly clear my reputation—yet an edict has abruptly descended and honors piled ever higher.
translations.idiomatic: I had meant to plead my sincerity before the court, step down from lofty rank, diminish the state's words about me, and slightly clear my reputation—yet an edict has abruptly descended and honors piled ever higher.

sentences.zh: 臣小人也，不及遠謀，寵利之來，何能居約，徒以上瀆天明，下汨彝議，災謫之興，懼必在邇。

translations.literal: Your servant is a small man, incapable of far-sighted counsel; favor and profit having come, how can I remain modest? I only profane heaven's clarity above and muddy public opinion below—the rise of calamity and reproof, I fear, is near.
translations.idiomatic: I am a small man, incapable of far-sighted counsel. Favor and profit having come, how can I remain modest? I only profane heaven's clarity above and muddy public opinion below—the rise of calamity and reproof, I fear, is near.

sentences.zh: 今之過授，以先微身，苟曰非據，危辱將及，十手所指，諭等膏肓，所以寤寐兢遽，維縈苦疾者也。

translations.literal: This excessive appointment, given my humble person—if the post is unearned, peril and disgrace will follow; when ten fingers point, the warning reaches the marrow; hence my waking and sleeping dread and ceaseless anguish.
translations.idiomatic: This excessive appointment, given my humble person—if the post is unearned, peril and disgrace will follow. When ten fingers point, the warning reaches the marrow; hence my waking and sleeping dread and ceaseless anguish.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下察其丹誠，矜其疾願，絕會收恩，以全愚分，則造化之施，方茲為薄。」

translations.literal: I humbly pray Your Majesty discern my sincere heart, pity my urgent plea, cease your grace and withdraw favor to preserve this fool's proper measure—even then your creative bounty would still seem excessive."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray Your Majesty discern my sincere heart, pity my urgent plea, cease your grace and withdraw favor to preserve this fool's proper measure—even then your creative bounty would still seem excessive.

sentences.zh: 見許。

translations.literal: His request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 時歲旱民饑，竣上言禁餳一月，息米近萬斛。

translations.literal: At the time drought and famine afflicted the people; Jun memorialized to forbid malt-sugar for one month, saving nearly ten thousand piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of drought and famine, Yan Jun memorialized to forbid malt-sugar for one month, saving nearly ten thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 復代謝莊為吏部尚書，領太子左衛率，未拜，丁憂。

translations.literal: Again to replace Xie Zhuang as Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, concurrently commanding Left Guard of the Heir Apparent—not yet taking office, entered mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was again to replace Xie Zhuang as Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and concurrently command the Left Guard of the Heir Apparent, but before taking office he entered mourning.

sentences.zh: 起為右將軍，丹陽尹如故。

translations.literal: Called back to serve as General of the Right; Magistrate of Danyang as before.
translations.idiomatic: Called back to serve as General of the Right while retaining the magistracy of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 竣藉蕃朝之舊，極陳得失。

translations.literal: Jun, relying on his long standing in the princely court, spoke to the utmost on gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on his long standing in the princely court, Yan Jun spoke freely on merits and flaws.

sentences.zh: 上自即吉之後，多所興造，竣諫爭懇切，無所回避，上意甚不說，多不見從。

translations.literal: After the emperor ended mourning, he undertook many constructions; Jun remonstrated earnestly without evasion—the emperor's intent very displeased, mostly not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period ended the emperor undertook many construction projects. Yan Jun remonstrated earnestly without evasion. The emperor was deeply displeased and often did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 竣自謂才足幹時，恩舊莫比，當贊務居中，永執朝政，而所陳多不被納，疑上欲疏之，乃求外出，以占時旨。

translations.literal: Jun considered his talent sufficient to serve the age and his favor unmatched; he expected to assist at court and hold power permanently—yet what he presented was mostly not accepted; suspecting the emperor meant to distance him, he sought an outside posting to test the times' intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun considered his talent sufficient to serve the age and his favor unmatched; he expected to assist at court and hold power permanently. When his counsel was often rejected he suspected the emperor meant to distance him, and sought an outside posting to test the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，以為東揚州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: First year of Daming, he was made Governor of Eastern Yang Province; general's rank as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daming he was appointed Governor of Eastern Yang Province, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 所求既許，便憂懼無計。

translations.literal: Once his request was granted, he was alarmed and at his wit's end.
translations.idiomatic: Once his request was granted, he was alarmed and at his wit's end.

sentences.zh: 至州，又丁母艱，不許去職，聽送喪還都，恩待猶厚，竣彌不自安。

translations.literal: On reaching the province he again mourned his mother—not permitted to leave office, allowed to escort the coffin back to the capital; favor remained lavish, and Jun grew ever more uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his province he again mourned his mother. He was not permitted to leave office but was allowed to escort the coffin to the capital. Favor remained lavish, and Yan Jun grew ever more uneasy.

sentences.zh: 每對親故，頗懷怨憤，又言朝事違謬，人主得失。

translations.literal: Whenever facing relatives and old friends, he often harbored resentment; again he spoke of court affairs as mistaken and the ruler's gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Among relatives and old friends he often voiced resentment, criticizing court affairs as mistaken and discussing the ruler's flaws.

sentences.zh: 及王僧達被誅，謂為竣所讒構，臨死陳竣前後忿懟，每恨言不見從。

translations.literal: When Wang Sengda was executed, it was said Jun had slandered and framed him; at death Wang cited Jun's successive resentments, each time regretting his words went unheeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sengda was executed, it was said Yan Jun had slandered him. At his death Wang cited Yan Jun's successive resentments and his constant regret that his words went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 僧達所言，頗有相符據。

translations.literal: What Wang Sengda said found considerable corroboration.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengda's statements found considerable corroboration.

sentences.zh: 上乃使御史中丞庾徽之奏之曰：

translations.literal: The emperor then had Supervising Censor Yin Huizhi impeach him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then had Supervising Censor Yin Huizhi impeach him, saying:

sentences.zh: :臣聞人臣之奉主，毀家光國，竭情無私，若乃無禮陵人，怙富卑上，是以王叔作戒，子晳為戮。

translations.literal: "Your servant has heard that ministers serving their lord should ruin their households to glorify the state and devote themselves without selfishness. Yet those who are rude and bully others, who rely on wealth to demean their superiors—for this Wang Shu was made a warning and Zixi was executed.
translations.idiomatic: "I have heard that ministers serving their lord should ruin their households to glorify the state and devote themselves without selfishness. Yet those who are rude and bully others, who rely on wealth to demean their superiors—for this Wang Shu was made a warning and Zixi was executed.

sentences.zh: 未有背本塞原，好利忘義，而得自容盛世，溷亂清流者也。

translations.literal: Never has one who turned against his roots, blocked the source, loved profit and forgot righteousness, yet found ease in a flourishing age and muddied the clear current.
translations.idiomatic: Never has one who turned against his roots, blocked the source, loved profit and forgot righteousness, yet found ease in a flourishing age and muddied the clear current.

sentences.zh: 右將軍、東揚州刺史建城縣開國侯顏竣，因附風雲，謬蒙翼長，天地更造，拔以非次。

translations.literal: General of the Right, Governor of Eastern Yang Province, and Marquis of Jiancheng County Yan Jun, riding the winds of fortune, absurdly received nurturing growth; when heaven and earth were remade he was promoted out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Right, Governor of Eastern Yang Province, and Marquis of Jiancheng County Yan Jun, riding the winds of fortune, absurdly received nurturing growth; when heaven and earth were remade he was promoted out of turn.

sentences.zh: 聖朝親攬，萬務一歸，而窺覘國柄，潛圖秉執。

translations.literal: The sacred court personally handled affairs and all matters returned to one authority, yet he spied on the handle of state power and secretly plotted to grasp and wield it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally handled affairs and concentrated all power in his own hands, yet Yan Jun watched for a chance at the reins of government and secretly plotted to seize them.

sentences.zh: 受任選曹，驅扇滋甚，出尹京輦，形勢彌放。

translations.literal: Assigned to the Selection Bureau, his agitation grew ever worse; sent out to govern the capital region, his power grew ever more unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Once placed in charge of personnel appointments, his factional agitation grew worse still; when he was sent out to govern the capital region, his arrogance became utterly unchecked.

sentences.zh: 傳詔犯憲，舊須啟聞，而竣以通訴忤己，輒加鞭辱，罔顧威靈，莫此為甚。

translations.literal: Imperial edict couriers who violated regulations formerly had to report to the throne, yet Jun, because a courier's report opposed him, immediately had them whipped and humiliated, heedless of imperial majesty—nothing surpassed this.
translations.idiomatic: Couriers bearing imperial edicts who broke regulations had always been required to report to the throne, but Yan Jun had any courier whose report displeased him whipped and humiliated on the spot, utterly heedless of imperial authority—nothing could exceed this.

sentences.zh: 嚴詔屢發，當官責效，竣權恣不行，怨懟彌起，懷挾姦數，苞藏陰慝。

translations.literal: Stern edicts issued repeatedly; officials were required to produce results. Jun arrogantly refused to comply, resentment grew ever stronger, he harbored treacherous schemes and concealed dark malice.
translations.idiomatic: Stern edicts were issued again and again and officials were held accountable for results, yet Yan Jun willfully refused to obey. Resentment mounted, he nursed treacherous designs, and concealed dark malice in his heart.

sentences.zh: 預聞中旨，罔不宣露，罰則委上，恩必歸己，荷遇之門，即加謗辱，受譴之室，曲相哀撫。

translations.literal: When he learned palace intent in advance, he always leaked it. Blame he put on the emperor; credit he kept for himself. At the door of those favored he added slander and insult; in the rooms of those punished he contrived consoling sympathy.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he learned the emperor's private intentions in advance, he always leaked them. He ascribed punishments to the throne but kept every favor for himself; at the homes of those in favor he spread slander and insult, while in the houses of those under censure he contrived sympathetic consolation.

sentences.zh: 翻戾朝紀，狡惑視聽，脅懼上宰，激動閭閻。

translations.literal: He overturned court discipline, cunningly confused what people heard and saw, intimidated the chief ministers, and stirred up the common folk.
translations.idiomatic: He subverted court order, cunningly misled what people heard and saw, intimidated the chief ministers, and stirred up the common people.

sentences.zh: 末慮上聞，內懷猜懼，偽請東牧，以卜天旨。

translations.literal: Fearing it would reach the emperor's ears, inwardly suspicious and afraid, he falsely requested governorship of the east to test heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid his conduct would reach the emperor's ears, he inwardly grew suspicious and fearful and falsely requested a provincial governorship in the east to test the throne's intent.

sentences.zh: 既獲出蕃，怨詈方肆，反脣腹誹，方之已輕。

translations.literal: Once posted outside the capital he cursed freely; muttering and slandering behind backs—the earlier criticism was mild by comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was posted outside the capital, his curses poured forth without restraint; muttering slander and speaking ill behind backs—what had gone before seemed mild by comparison.

sentences.zh: 且時有啟奏，必協姦私，宣示親朋，動作羣小。

translations.literal: Moreover, whenever memorials were submitted, he always colluded for private gain, showed them to kin and friends, and stirred up petty factions.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, whenever memorials were submitted to the throne, he always colluded for private ends, showed them to kin and friends, and stirred up petty factions.

sentences.zh: 前冬母亡，詔賜還葬，事畢不去，盤桓經時，方構間勳貴，造立同異。

translations.literal: The previous winter his mother died; an edict granted him leave to return and bury her. When the rites were done he would not leave, lingered for a long time, and only then sought to drive wedges among meritorious nobles and sow dissent.
translations.idiomatic: The previous winter his mother died. An edict granted him leave to return and bury her, but when the rites were finished he would not depart. He lingered for a long while, seeking to drive wedges among meritorious nobles and sow division.

sentences.zh: 又表示危懼，深營身觀，曲訪大臣，慮不全立，遂以己被斥外，國道將顛，釁積懷抱，惡窮辭色。

translations.literal: He also feigned terror, worked hard on self-preservation, probed senior ministers indirectly, fearing he might not survive intact; finding himself cast outside, he said the state's way would topple—grievances piled in his breast and malice showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: He also feigned terror, worked hard at self-preservation, and probed senior ministers indirectly, fearing he might not survive. Finding himself cast out, he claimed the nation's course was about to collapse; grievances piled in his breast and malice showed plainly on his face.

sentences.zh: 兼行闕於家，早負世議，逮身居崇寵，奉兼萬金，榮以夸親，祿不充養。

translations.literal: His conduct at home had long been wanting and drew public criticism; once he held supreme favor with income over ten thousand in cash, he flaunted glory before kin but would not use his salary to support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct at home had long been deficient and had drawn public censure. Once he held supreme favor with an income of more than ten thousand in cash, he flaunted his glory before kin yet would not use his salary to support his parents.

sentences.zh: 宿憾母弟，恃貴輒戮，天倫怨毒，親交震駭。

translations.literal: Old grudge against his younger brother of the same mother—relying on rank he killed him; family bonds turned poisonous and friends and kin were shocked.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing an old grudge against his younger brother by the same mother, he relied on his rank to have him killed. Family bonds turned poisonous and friends and kin were appalled.

sentences.zh: 凡所莅任，皆闕政刑，輒開丹陽庫物，貸借吏下。

translations.literal: In every post he held he neglected governance and law, opening Danyang storehouse goods to lend to subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: In every office he held he neglected governance and law, opening goods from the Danyang treasury to lend to his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 多假資禮，解為門生，充朝滿野，殆將千計。

translations.literal: He often feigned gift-money, taking men as disciples—they filled court and countryside, nearly a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He often made pretense of gift payments and took men on as disciples; they filled the court and the countryside, numbering nearly a thousand.

sentences.zh: 驕放自下，妨公害私，取監解見錢，以供帳下。

translations.literal: Arrogance from below, harming the public for private gain—he seized cash held under escrow to supply his personal staff.
translations.idiomatic: Arrogant from the bottom up, he harmed the public for private gain, seizing cash held in escrow to supply his personal staff.

sentences.zh: 賓旅酣歌，不異平月，街談道說，非復風聲。

translations.literal: Guests and travelers sang drunk as in ordinary months; street talk and gossip were no longer the proper tone.
translations.idiomatic: Guests and travelers sang and drank as freely as in ordinary months; street talk and gossip no longer reflected the proper tone of public life.

sentences.zh: :竣代都文吏，特荷天私，棄瑕錄用，豫參要重，勞無汗馬，賞班河、山，出內寵靈，踰越倫伍。

translations.literal: Jun rose from a clerk in the capital office, especially favored by heaven's partiality; flaws set aside, he was employed and joined great affairs in advance. Labor without sweating horse—reward matched rivers and mountains; favor from within and without exceeded his rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun rose from a clerk in the capital administration and was especially favored by heaven's partiality; his flaws were set aside and he was employed, joining weighty affairs in advance. He performed no labor worthy of a sweating horse, yet his rewards matched rivers and mountains; favor from within and without placed him beyond his proper rank.

sentences.zh: 山川之性，日月彌滋，溪壑之心，在盈彌奓，虎冠狼貪，未足為譬。

translations.literal: The nature of mountains and rivers: day by day more nourished. The heart of streams and gorges: the fuller, the more swollen. Tiger-cap wolf-greed is insufficient as comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Like mountains and rivers, he grew more insatiable with each passing day; like streams and gorges, the more he had, the more he swelled. Even the tiger's cap and the wolf's greed are insufficient as comparison.

sentences.zh: 今皇明開耀，品物咸亨，傷俗點化，實唯害焉，宜加顯戮，以彰盛化。

translations.literal: Now imperial brilliance shines forth and all things prosper; he harms custom and stains civilization—it is truly harm alone. Public execution should be added to manifest flourishing transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Now that imperial brilliance shines forth and all things flourish, he harms custom and stains civilization—he is truly nothing but harm. He should receive public execution to manifest the greatness of our age.

sentences.zh: 請以見事免竣所居官，下太常削爵土，須事御收付廷尉法獄罪。

translations.literal: I request that he be immediately dismissed from his offices, that the Minister of Ceremonials be instructed to strip his rank and fief, and that upon the matter he be handed over to the Minister of Justice for legal imprisonment and trial.
translations.idiomatic: I request that he be immediately dismissed from all his offices, that the Minister of Ceremonials be instructed to strip his rank and fief, and that he then be handed over to the Minister of Justice for trial in the legal prison.

sentences.zh: 上未欲便加大戮，且止免官。

translations.literal: The emperor did not yet wish to impose capital punishment; he only dismissed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not yet wish to impose capital punishment and only dismissed him from office.

sentences.zh: 竣頻啟謝罪，并乞性命。

translations.literal: Jun repeatedly submitted apologies and also begged for his life.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun repeatedly submitted apologies and also begged for his life.

sentences.zh: 上愈怒，詔答曰：「憲司所奏，非宿昔所以相期。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angrier still and replied by edict: "What the censorate reports is not what we long expected.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angrier still and replied by edict: "What the censorate reports is not what we long expected.

sentences.zh: 卿受榮遇，故當極此，訕訐怨憤，已孤本望，乃復過煩思慮，懼不自全，豈為下事上誠節之至邪！」

translations.literal: You received honor and favor—you ought to have gone to the utmost of this. Slander, remonstrance, and resentment have already betrayed my hope. And yet you again over-trouble your thoughts, fearing you cannot preserve yourself—is this the utmost sincerity of a subordinate serving his superior!"
translations.idiomatic: You received honor and favor—you ought to have gone to the utmost in loyalty. Slander, remonstrance, and resentment have already betrayed my hopes. And yet you again trouble yourself with anxious thoughts, fearing you cannot preserve yourself—is this the utmost sincerity of a subordinate serving his superior!"

sentences.zh: 及竟陵王誕為逆，因此陷之，召御史中丞庾徽之於前為奏，奏成，詔曰：「竣孤負恩養，乃可至此。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jingling Dan rebelled, the emperor used this to frame him. He summoned Supervising Censor Yu Huizhi before him to draft the memorial. When it was done, the edict said: "Jun betrayed nurtured favor—how could it come to this?
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Jingling Liu Dan rebelled, the emperor used this to frame Yan Jun. He summoned Supervising Censor Yu Huizhi before him to draft the memorial. When it was done, the edict said: "Yan Jun betrayed the favor with which he was nurtured—how could it come to this?

sentences.zh: 於獄賜死，妻息宥之以遠。」

translations.literal: He was granted death in prison; wife and children were spared and sent far away."
translations.idiomatic: He was granted death in prison; his wife and children were spared and exiled to a distant place."

sentences.zh: 子辟強徙送交州，又於道殺之。

translations.literal: His son Biqiang was exiled to Jiaozhou and was killed on the road as well.
translations.idiomatic: His son Biqiang was exiled to Jiaozhou and was killed on the road as well.

sentences.zh: 竣文集行於世。

translations.literal: Jun's collected writings circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun's collected writings circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historical Appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Historical Appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：世祖弱歲臨蕃，涵道未廣，披胸解帶，義止賓僚。

translations.literal: The historian says: When Emperor Shizu was young at his princedom, his grasp of the Way was not yet broad; baring breast and loosening belt—the meaning stopped at fellow guests and staff.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: When Emperor Shizu was young at his princedom, his grasp of the Way was not yet broad; opening his heart and loosening his belt meant no more than intimacy among guests and staff.

sentences.zh: 及運鍾傾陂，身危慮切，擢膽抽肝，猶患言未盡也。

translations.literal: When fate struck at the tipping slope and his person was in peril with anxious thoughts acute, he pulled gall and drew liver—still fearing his words were not fully spoken.
translations.idiomatic: When fate struck at the tipping point and his person was in peril with anxious thoughts acute, he poured out gall and liver—yet still feared his words were not fully spoken.

sentences.zh: 至於馮玉負扆，威行萬物，欲有必從，事無暫失。

translations.literal: As for leaning on jade and resting against the screen, authority moved all things—what he wished was always obeyed, affairs never briefly missed.
translations.idiomatic: Once he leaned on the jade mat and rested against the imperial screen, his authority moved all things—what he wished was always obeyed and affairs never briefly went awry.

sentences.zh: 既而憂歡異日，甘苦變心，主挾今情，臣追昔款，宋昌之報，上賞已行，同舟之慮，下望愈結，嫌怨既萌，誅責自起。

translations.literal: Then joy and sorrow differed by day, sweet and bitter changed hearts—the lord held present feeling, the minister recalled past warmth. Song Chang's reward: the upper honor was already given; shared-boat anxiety: the lower hope grew ever tighter. Suspicion and resentment once sprouted, punishment and blame arose of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Then joy and sorrow differed by day and sweet turned to bitter in their hearts—the lord held to present feeling while the minister recalled past warmth. The reward owed to Song Chang: the emperor's favor had already been given; the anxiety of sharing one boat: the minister's hopes grew ever tighter. Once suspicion and resentment took root, punishment and blame arose of themselves.

sentences.zh: 竣之取釁於世，蓋由此乎。

translations.literal: That Yan Jun met his downfall in the world—probably from this?
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun's downfall in the world probably stemmed from this.

sentences.zh: 為人臣者，若能事主而捐其私，立功而忘其報，雖求顛陷，不可得也。

translations.literal: As a minister, if one can serve the lord and cast aside private interest, establish merit and forget reward—even seeking ruin, one could not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: For one who serves as minister, if he can serve his lord and cast aside private interest, establish merit and forget reward—even if he sought ruin, he could not obtain it.
